checklist.step: Freeze the quarter-end in-force extract from policy administration
actions: On reference date +2 business days run the scheduled quarter-end in-force job, restricted to the UK Life and Annuities writing entity and the reference date position.

Extract per contract: policy number, product code, Solvency II line of business, status, commencement date, annuity in payment or sum assured, premium, guarantee period, life status and last transaction date.
Record the run identifier, row count and the sum of annuity in payment and sum assured on the extract control sheet and lock the extract folder to read-only.
Hand the control sheet to the Valuation Actuary and the Data Quality Analyst by email the same day so no downstream team recomputes its own totals.
checklist.done: the extract is locked, carries a run identifier and a signed control sheet with row count and benefit totals.

checklist.step: Load the extract into the actuarial data mart and prove nothing was lost in transit
actions: Run the quarter-end ingestion pipeline into the actuarial data mart and capture rows read, rows rejected and rows written for every stage.
Compare rows written and the benefit totals against the Policy Admin Ops Lead control sheet, cell for cell, before any transformation is applied.
List every rejected row with its rejection reason (null commencement date, unmapped product code, duplicate policy number) in the load exception file.
Publish the load report to the Valuation Actuary and refuse to release the mart to modelling until rejects are zero or individually accepted in writing.
checklist.done: loaded rows and benefit totals equal the source control sheet, with every reject listed and dispositioned.

checklist.step: Reconcile contract counts by product and line of business to policy administration
actions: Build the reconciliation grid with one row per product code and Solvency II line of business (other life insurance, insurance with profit participation, annuities stemming from non-life contracts as applicable).
Enter the policy admin count, the data mart count and the difference for each grid row, plus opening count, new business, deaths, surrenders, maturities and transfers as the movement bridge.
Trace every non-zero difference to a named cause and record the policy numbers behind it; never net one product difference against another.
Send the grid to the Valuation Actuary with each unexplained difference flagged red.
checklist.done: each product and line of business row reconciles to zero or carries a named cause with the underlying policy numbers.

checklist.step: Reconcile benefit and premium amounts to the general ledger
actions: Pull the quarter-to-date premium income, annuity payments and claims paid balances for the UK Life and Annuities entity from the general ledger trial balance at the reference date.
Compare them to the equivalent aggregates from the actuarial data mart extract and record the difference in absolute terms and as a percentage of the ledger balance.
Split each difference into timing (cash booked after the extract cut), scope (reinsurance ceded, non-modelled products) and error, and evidence each split with a journal or transaction listing.
Sign the ledger tie-out sheet and return it to the Valuation Actuary for inclusion in the reconciliation pack.
checklist.done: premium, annuity payment and claims aggregates tie to the ledger with every difference split into timing, scope or error.

checklist.step: Run the data quality rule set over the loaded extract
actions: Execute the technical provisions rule pack: mandatory field completeness, date of birth plausibility (age 0 to 120), commencement date not after the reference date, positive annuity amount, valid product and line of business codes, and duplicate policy number detection.
Score each rule against its tolerance and produce the accuracy, completeness and appropriateness summary the PRA Reporting Part expects the firm to hold.
Export the failed record list per rule with policy numbers and route it to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for source correction rather than downstream patching.
Record rules that failed but are accepted for the quarter, with the accepted impact quantified in policies and benefit amount.
checklist.done: every rule has a score against tolerance and each failure is either corrected at source or accepted with a quantified impact.

checklist.step: Clear the reconciliation breaks and record what could not be cleared
actions: Open the break log and give each break an owner from Policy Admin Operations, Finance or the actuarial team, plus a target clearance date inside the close calendar.
For each break record the policy count, the benefit amount and the estimated effect on the best estimate liability so materiality is a number, not an opinion.
Compare the total uncleared benefit amount to the 0.1 per cent of best estimate liability tolerance and escalate to the Chief Actuary the moment it is breached.
Close each break with the corrective action taken and the evidence reference; leave nothing closed as resolved without a linked correction.
checklist.done: every break is owned, quantified against the best estimate liability and either cleared with evidence or escalated.

checklist.step: Build the model point file and tie it back to the cleared extract
actions: Run the model point generation routine that groups the cleared extract into Prophet model points by product, age band, gender, guarantee term and payment frequency.
Produce the grouping reconciliation: number of contracts in, number of model points out, and total annuity in payment and sum assured in versus out.
Investigate any amount difference above the grouping tolerance of 0.01 per cent and correct the grouping keys rather than plugging a balancing model point.
Save the model point file and its reconciliation into the valuation run folder named by reference date and run identifier.
checklist.done: the model point file reproduces the cleared extract benefit totals within 0.01 per cent with a documented grouping reconciliation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the technical provisions movement against the prior quarter
actions: Produce the analysis of change from the prior reference date best estimate liability to the current one, split into expected unwind, new business, experience variance, assumption changes, model changes and economic or risk-free curve movement.
Reconcile the data-driven components back to the contract count and benefit movements in the reconciliation grid so a fall in reserves is explained by real policy exits.
Challenge any component above 1 per cent of opening best estimate liability with the modelling owner and record the explanation in the analysis of change commentary.
Circulate the analysis of change to the Chief Actuary and the Capital Model Actuary ahead of the reserve review meeting.
checklist.done: the movement in best estimate liability is fully attributed and the data-driven components agree with the reconciliation grid.

checklist.step: Tie the reconciled figures into the UK Quantitative Reporting Templates
actions: Populate S.02.01 balance sheet technical provisions, S.12.01 life and health SLT technical provisions and S.17.01 where non-life SLT annuities apply, from the signed valuation run only.
Build the tie-out sheet mapping each reported cell to the reconciliation pack line and the valuation run identifier that produced it.
Run the Bank of England Insurance XBRL taxonomy validations for the reporting period and clear every blocking rule before the pack leaves the reporting team.
Send the tie-out sheet plus the validation output to the Valuation Actuary for confirmation that the reported numbers are the reconciled numbers.
checklist.done: every technical provisions cell in S.02.01, S.12.01 and S.17.01 maps to a reconciliation pack line and passes taxonomy validation.

checklist.step: Write the quarterly data quality statement required by the Reporting Part
actions: Draft the statement covering accuracy, completeness and appropriateness of the technical provisions data, citing the rule scores, the reconciliation results and the accepted exceptions.
List the data limitations carried into the valuation and the compensating actuarial judgements applied, with the actuary who applied each one named.
Update the data directory entry for each in-scope field so the lineage from policy administration field to QRT cell is documented for the PRA.
Route the statement to the Chief Actuary and the Chief Risk Officer for review before sign-off.
checklist.done: a dated data quality statement exists naming rule scores, accepted limitations and the judgements applied.

checklist.step: Hold the reserve review meeting and record the challenge
actions: Convene the quarterly reserve review with the Valuation Actuary, Reserving Actuary, Controller and Chief Risk Officer at reference date +18 business days.
Walk the reconciliation grid, the ledger tie-out, the break log and the analysis of change, and require an answer on every red-flagged difference.
Minute each challenge, the response and any action with an owner and a date, and record whether the technical provisions are accepted for reporting.
Withhold acceptance where an uncleared break exceeds tolerance and set the resubmission plan instead.
checklist.done: minuted challenge exists for every red-flagged difference and the technical provisions are formally accepted or held.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial function opinion on data used for technical provisions
actions: Read the reconciliation pack, the data quality statement and the accepted limitations against the Conditions Governing Business 6 duty to assess the sufficiency and quality of data.
State in writing whether the data is sufficient and of adequate quality for the calculation of technical provisions at this reference date.
Where it is not, specify the deficiency, the affected line of business and the recommendation to the board, and copy the Chief Risk Officer.
File the signed opinion into the valuation run folder as part of the quarter-end record.
checklist.done: a signed actuarial function opinion on data sufficiency and quality exists for the reference date.

checklist.step: Submit the reporting pack to the PRA through BEEDS inside the deadline
actions: Compute the deadline as reference date plus 30 business days for the quarterly submission or plus 70 business days for the 31 December annual submission under PS15/24, and post it on the close calendar.
Log in to the Bank of England BEEDS portal, open the insurance solo return for the reference period and upload the validated XBRL instance for the QRT and National Specific Template set.
Clear any BEEDS validation error, resubmit, and save the submission receipt with its BEEDS reference number and timestamp.
Circulate the receipt to the Chief Actuary, the Chief Financial Officer and the Corporate Secretary as proof of timely filing.
checklist.done: BEEDS shows an accepted submission for the reference period with a receipt filed before the 30 or 70 business day deadline.

checklist.step: Raise data quality incidents for anything that survived the close
actions: Open an incident for every break accepted above tolerance, every failed data quality rule accepted for the quarter and every late milestone in the close calendar.
Record the root cause category (source system defect, mapping gap, manual adjustment, late data from a third-party administrator) and the owning function.
Set the remediation date inside the next quarter and link the incident to the affected QRT cell so recurrence is visible at the next close.
Report the open incident list to the Risk Committee with the aggregate benefit amount exposed.
checklist.done: each accepted exception has an incident with a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a linked QRT cell.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation pack under the retention rule
actions: Deposit the extract control sheet, load report, reconciliation grid, ledger tie-out, break log, model point reconciliation, data quality statement, actuarial opinion, QRT tie-out and BEEDS receipt as one indexed pack.
Name the pack by entity and reference date and apply the 10-year retention label measured from the reference date.
Confirm the repository index makes the pack searchable by reference date, QRT template code and BEEDS reference number.
Grant read access to Internal Audit and the external auditor without allowing edits to the filed pack.
checklist.done: the pack is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by reference date and QRT template code.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of in-scope contracts independently of the actuarial team
actions: Run your own read-only query against policy administration for all contracts in force at the reference date for the UK Life and Annuities entity, without using the actuarial extract.
Capture your row count, total annuity in payment and total sum assured, and compare them to the frozen extract control sheet.
Investigate any difference before sampling, including contracts written on the reference date and contracts lapsed with an effective date in the period.
Sign the population as complete and record the query text in the workpaper so it can be re-run.
testing.done: an independently built population reconciles to the frozen extract and the query is recorded for re-performance.

testing.step: Reconcile the reported QRT technical provisions back to the source of record
actions: Take the submitted S.12.01 and S.02.01 technical provisions figures from the BEEDS submission copy rather than the draft pack.
Walk the chain backwards: reported cell to valuation run output to model point file to cleared extract to policy administration, capturing each figure at each hop.
Confirm the valuation run identifier on the QRT tie-out sheet is the run that produced the submitted numbers and not a superseded run.
Record any hop where the figure changes without a documented reason as an exception.
testing.done: each submitted technical provisions figure traces hop by hop to policy administration with no undocumented change.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible policy sample
actions: Take 100 per cent of contracts with an annuity in payment above GBP 100,000 a year and all contracts touched by a manual adjustment during the close.
Take 40 further contracts by seeded random selection across product and line of business strata from the remaining population.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratum boundaries and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Store the sample list in the workpaper before any testing begins.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers all large annuities and manually adjusted contracts.

testing.step: Vouch sampled policy data back to the administration record
actions: Open each sampled policy in the administration system and read date of birth, commencement date, annuity amount or sum assured, payment frequency, guarantee period and status.
Compare each field to the extract row and to the model point that carries the policy, noting the model point identifier.
For any field difference, determine whether the extract, the mapping or the source is wrong and quantify the effect on the best estimate liability.
Screenshot the administration screen for every exception into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled policy agrees field by field with the administration record or the difference is quantified and captured.

testing.step: Re-perform the grouping reconciliation into model points
actions: Take the cleared extract and independently aggregate annuity in payment and sum assured by the documented grouping keys.
Compare your totals to the model point file totals and compute the grouping difference as a percentage of the extract total.
Test the 0.01 per cent grouping tolerance and confirm no balancing or plug model point exists in the file.
Report any grouping key applied in the model that is not described in the documented methodology.
testing.done: the independently aggregated totals match the model point file within tolerance with no plug model point present.

testing.step: Re-perform the general ledger tie-out
actions: Pull the premium income, annuity payment and claims paid balances at the reference date directly from the trial balance for the entity.
Recompute the difference to the actuarial aggregates and re-derive the timing, scope and error split from the supporting journals.
Test that scope differences are genuinely out of the technical provisions boundary rather than omitted business.
Treat any unexplained residual above GBP 5 million or 0.1 per cent of best estimate liability as a fail.
testing.done: the ledger difference is independently re-derived and the residual sits inside the stated threshold.

testing.step: Test the data quality rule set for coverage as well as results
actions: List every field used in the technical provisions calculation and check each one is covered by at least one completeness and one validity rule.
Re-run three rules on the frozen extract and compare your failure counts to the reported rule scores.
Read the accepted exception list and confirm each acceptance carries a quantified impact and an approver, not a blanket sign-off.
Flag any field that drives the best estimate liability and has no rule as a control gap.
testing.done: every calculation field has rule coverage, re-run rule counts agree, and each acceptance is quantified and approved.

testing.step: Recompute the submission deadline and prove the filing was timely
actions: Recompute the deadline from the reference date using the UK business day calendar: 30 business days for the quarterly return and 70 business days for the 31 December annual return.
Read the BEEDS submission receipt timestamp and reference number and compare it to the recomputed deadline.
Where a resubmission occurred, identify what changed, why, and whether the original submission was materially wrong.
Record any submission after the deadline as a reportable breach of the Reporting Part rather than a test exception.
testing.done: the deadline is recomputed and the BEEDS receipt proves submission on or before it, with resubmissions explained.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception carrying the reference date, the affected policies or QRT cells and the quantified best estimate liability impact.
Assign a root cause from source system defect, mapping error, manual adjustment without evidence, late third-party administrator data or missing rule coverage.
Set an owner and a remediation date inside the next reporting cycle and require a retest at the next quarter-end.
Escalate any exception affecting a submitted QRT figure to the Chief Actuary within two business days for a resubmission decision.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, quantified impact, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Compute the exception rate against the sample and compare the aggregate unexplained difference to the 0.1 per cent of best estimate liability threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, referencing the workpaper sections that support it.
Have the reviewer who prepared no part of the reconciliation sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and open breaches to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with an exception rate, a stated conclusion and a dated Audit Committee reporting reference.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns every PRA inquiry touching technical provisions, transitional measures, matching adjustment or the annual actuarial opinion; the Regulatory Reporting Manager runs the logistics and the deadline clock

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 6 (actuarial function) and the Reporting Part read together with section 165 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 information-gathering powers and Fundamental Rule 7 (open and cooperative dealing), re-read on receipt of each inquiry

In-scope processes.value: Inbound PRA supervisory correspondence on valuation: periodic summary meeting follow-ups, QRT data queries, matching adjustment and transitional measure on technical provisions questions, and section 166 skilled person information requests

In-scope systems.value: Inquiries arrive from the named PRA supervisor by email or through the BEEDS portal; every item is registered in the regulatory correspondence register with the response due date and the evidence attached

Compliance procedure documented.value: PRA Valuation Inquiry Response Procedure — registration, two business day acknowledgement, question decomposition, evidence sourcing from the signed valuation run, actuarial and legal review, SMF sign-off, submission and follow-up tracking

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the General Counsel, reviewed annually and after every PRA periodic summary meeting or supervisory letter that changes the expected response route

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The date stated in the PRA letter governs; where none is stated the internal standard is 15 business days, acknowledgement within 2 business days, and extensions requested in writing at least 5 business days before the stated date

Deadline reminders configured.value: The correspondence register raises reminders at due date minus 10, minus 5 and minus 2 business days to the Appointed Actuary and the Regulatory Reporting Manager, with automatic escalation to the Chief Actuary at minus 2

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Inquiry letter, the working file, every draft, the model run identifiers relied on, the sign-offs and the sent response retained 10 years from the response date so the answer can be reconstructed exactly

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any response sent after the stated date, any answer later found to be incorrect, and any commitment made to the PRA that is missed is logged as a regulatory relationship issue with root cause and correction

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The SMF4 Chief Risk Officer signs off any correction issued to the PRA and any remediation arising from an inaccurate or late valuation answer

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All PRA and skilled person inquiries touching valuation, technical provisions or the actuarial function received in the period, taken from the regulatory correspondence register and the Appointed Actuary mailbox

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed stated deadlines and on uncleared commitments; any answer not traceable to a signed valuation run or a documented judgement is a fail; more than one fail escalates to the Board Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is event-driven, so the test runs semi-annually over every inquiry received in the half-year plus 100 per cent of inquiries carrying a follow-up commitment

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, reviewed or signed any sampled response and does not report into the actuarial function

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual regulatory inquiry response test workpaper (register extract, mailbox completeness check, sampled working files, re-performed calculations, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Correspondence register export with dates received, dates responded, commitments and closure evidence, producible to the PRA supervisor or a skilled person within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: All valuation correspondence goes out through the Regulatory Reporting Manager to the named PRA supervisory contact; the General Counsel clears any answer that admits an error before it is sent

checklist.step: Register the inquiry the day it arrives and start the clock
actions: Create a register entry the day the letter or BEEDS message lands, recording the PRA sender and supervisory contact, date received, the powers relied on (routine supervision or section 165), the stated response date and the reference number quoted.
Attach the original letter and every enclosure unaltered, and record how it arrived so the channel for the reply is fixed.
Compute the response due date from the stated date, or from the internal 15 business day standard where none is stated, and set the minus 10, minus 5 and minus 2 business day reminders.
Notify the Appointed Actuary, the Chief Actuary and the General Counsel within the same working day.
checklist.done: the inquiry has a register entry with sender, date received, due date, reminders and the original letter attached.

checklist.step: Acknowledge receipt to the PRA supervisor within two business days
actions: Reply to the named supervisor confirming receipt, quoting their reference, naming the Appointed Actuary as the responsible individual and confirming the date you will respond.
Where the stated date is not achievable, say so in this acknowledgement and propose a specific alternative date with the reason, rather than going quiet.
Copy the Chief Actuary, the Chief Risk Officer and the General Counsel on the acknowledgement.
File the sent acknowledgement against the register entry.
checklist.done: a dated acknowledgement naming the responsible individual and the response date is sent and filed within two business days.

checklist.step: Decompose the letter into individually answerable questions
actions: Split the letter into numbered sub-questions, one per fact, figure or opinion sought, and enter each on the response matrix.

Tag each sub-question with the subject (best estimate liability, risk margin, matching adjustment portfolio, transitional measure on technical provisions, contract boundaries under Technical Provisions 3, assumption setting, data quality).
Assign an owner and an internal draft date at least five business days before the PRA due date.
Mark which sub-questions require a model re-run and start those first because they carry the longest lead time.
checklist.done: every sub-question has a number, subject tag, named owner and internal draft date on the response matrix.

checklist.step: Identify the exact reporting position the questions relate to
actions: Establish the reference date behind the question and pull the corresponding submitted QRT set and BEEDS receipt so you answer on the numbers the PRA holds.
Record the valuation run identifier, model version, assumption set version and risk-free curve used at that reference date.
Confirm whether any resubmission has occurred since, and if so state which version the answer describes.
Lock a read-only copy of that run output into the inquiry working file.
checklist.done: the answer is anchored to a named reference date, valuation run identifier, model version and assumption set.

checklist.step: Pull the underlying data and calculations from the signed valuation record
actions: Extract from the locked run the cash flow projections, model point groupings, assumption tables and reconciliations that bear on each sub-question.

Where the PRA asks for a split not produced in the original run (by line of business, cohort, guarantee type), produce it from the same run rather than a new one, and label it as a re-cut not a re-run.
Record every figure with its source cell reference so a reviewer can find it without asking you.
Save the extracts into the inquiry working file under the sub-question number.
checklist.done: each sub-question has supporting extracts drawn from the locked run and labelled with source references.

checklist.step: Re-run the model only where the question requires a new calculation
actions: Where the PRA asks for a sensitivity or an alternative basis, set up the run from the locked production run and change only the parameters named in the question.
Record the run identifier, the parameters changed, the parameters deliberately held, and the run date in the model change log.
Reconcile the new run to the production run on the unchanged components so any difference is attributable to the requested change alone.
Have the Model Risk Manager review the run set-up before the results go into the draft answer.
checklist.done: each requested calculation has its own run identifier, a parameter change log and a reconciliation to the production run.

checklist.step: Draft the answers with the citation and the caveat attached to each one
actions: Write each answer against its sub-question number, opening with the direct answer and then the basis, in plain language a supervisor can read without the model documentation.
Cite the rule the answer engages, for example Technical Provisions 3 for contract boundaries or the Reporting Part for data quality, and the reference date the figures come from.
State every limitation, approximation and expert judgement relied on, with who made it and when, instead of leaving it to be discovered later.
Never answer a question the PRA did not ask, and never leave a sub-question with no answer text.
checklist.done: every numbered sub-question has a drafted answer with its basis, citation, reference date and stated limitations.

checklist.step: Peer review the numbers before anyone else reads the draft
actions: Take each figure in the draft and trace it independently to the run output or the submitted QRT cell it claims to come from.
Recompute every derived figure quoted in the text, including percentages, ratios and movements, and initial each one on the review sheet.
Challenge any statement of methodology against the technical provisions methodology document and require alignment or an explicit explanation of the difference.
Return the draft with review points and re-check the corrections rather than accepting a verbal confirmation.
checklist.done: every figure and derived number in the draft is traced or recomputed and initialled on a review sheet.

checklist.step: Route the draft for legal and risk review
actions: Read the draft for any admission of a rule breach, any statement of future intention, and any wording that could be read as a commitment the firm has not agreed to.
Confirm the response is consistent with prior correspondence on the same subject by checking the register history for the same topic tag.
Mark anything that must be pre-cleared with the General Counsel and hold those paragraphs until cleared.
Record the legal clearance and its date on the register entry.
checklist.done: the draft carries dated legal clearance and no uncleared admission or forward commitment remains.

checklist.step: Obtain the accountable senior manager sign-off
actions: Review the response matrix, the peer review sheet and the legal clearance together before signing.
Confirm the answers are consistent with the actuarial function report and with the last ORSA submitted to the PRA.
Sign the response with name, senior management function reference and date, and record any answer you have modified before signing.
Refuse sign-off where a sub-question is unanswered or a figure has no traced source, and send it back with the specific gap named.
checklist.done: the response carries a dated senior manager signature and no unanswered sub-question or untraced figure remains.

checklist.step: Send the response through the agreed channel and prove delivery
actions: Send the response to the named PRA supervisory contact by the channel the inquiry arrived through, quoting their reference and listing the enclosures by name.
Where the PRA specified BEEDS, upload the response and the annexes to the correct return or ad hoc data request slot and save the submission receipt.
Record the sent date and time, the delivery evidence and the enclosure list on the register entry, and compare the sent date against the due date.
Circulate the sent response to the Chief Actuary, Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel the same day.
checklist.done: the response is sent by the agreed channel with delivery evidence and the sent date recorded against the due date.

checklist.step: Open a commitment record for anything promised in the response
actions: Extract every forward-looking statement from the sent response, such as a methodology change, a data remediation or a further analysis to be provided.
Create a commitment record for each with the wording used to the PRA, the owner, the date promised and the evidence that will close it.
Report open regulatory commitments to the Risk Committee monthly until closed, showing days remaining against the promised date.
Escalate any commitment at risk to the Chief Risk Officer at least ten business days before the promised date so the PRA can be told before it slips.
checklist.done: every promise made to the PRA has a commitment record with owner, promised date and closure evidence defined.

checklist.step: Handle follow-up questions as new entries on the same thread
actions: Register each PRA follow-up as its own entry linked to the parent inquiry so the thread history stays intact and its own due date is tracked.
Re-read the original answer before responding and state plainly where the new answer supersedes or corrects the earlier one.
Where the follow-up shows the original answer was wrong, issue a correction proactively with the corrected figure and the cause, cleared by the General Counsel.
Close the thread only when the PRA confirms no further questions or the register entry is marked closed with the supervisor's last message attached.
checklist.done: every follow-up is linked, separately tracked and answered, and corrections are issued proactively where needed.

checklist.step: Feed the inquiry back into the valuation control environment
actions: Review the inquiry at the Risk Committee and decide whether it signals a control weakness, a disclosure gap or a supervisory concern about the actuarial function.
Where it does, raise an action to change the technical provisions methodology, the QRT preparation controls or the SFCR narrative for the next cycle.
Record the supervisory theme so the next periodic summary meeting preparation covers it with evidence already assembled.
Report themes and trends in PRA valuation inquiries to the Board Risk Committee at least annually.
checklist.done: the inquiry has a recorded control decision and, where a weakness exists, an owned change to methodology or controls.

checklist.step: File the complete working file under the retention rule
actions: Deposit the original letter, response matrix, extracts, run identifiers, peer review sheet, legal clearance, signed response, delivery evidence and follow-up thread as one indexed file.
Name the file by PRA reference and response date and apply the 10-year retention label measured from the response date.
Confirm the file is searchable by PRA reference, reference date and subject tag so a future skilled person review can find it.
Grant read-only access to Internal Audit and the actuarial function without allowing edits after filing.
checklist.done: the working file is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by PRA reference and subject tag.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation inquiries independently of the register
actions: Search the Appointed Actuary, Chief Actuary and regulatory mailbox for correspondence from PRA domains in the half-year and list every item touching valuation or technical provisions.
Add every BEEDS ad hoc data request and every skilled person information request for the same period.
Reconcile your list to the regulatory correspondence register and treat any inquiry present in a mailbox but absent from the register as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete and record the search terms and date ranges in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently built inquiry population is reconciled to the register with unregistered items listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Recompute every response deadline and test timeliness
actions: Read the stated response date from each original PRA letter rather than the register field, and apply the 15 business day internal standard only where the letter states none.
Recompute the elapsed business days from date received to date sent using the UK business day calendar.
Compare the acknowledgement date to the two business day standard for every inquiry in the population.
List every late acknowledgement and every late response, and check whether an extension was requested in writing at least five business days ahead.
testing.done: deadlines are recomputed from the source letters and every late acknowledgement or response is listed with its extension evidence.

testing.step: Select the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100 per cent of inquiries that carried a forward commitment, alleged an error, or were issued under section 165 or a skilled person review.
Take 10 further inquiries by seeded random selection from the remaining population, minimum 15 in total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Fix the sample in the workpaper before opening any working file.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and includes every commitment-bearing and formally powered inquiry.

testing.step: Re-perform the key valuation judgement behind each sampled answer
actions: Open the run identifier cited in the sampled response and reproduce the figure quoted to the PRA from the run output without reading the draft first.
For sensitivity answers, confirm only the named parameters were changed by reading the model change log for that run.
Compare your reproduced figure to the figure sent; any difference, including rounding presented as exact, is an exception.
Capture the run output screen or extract into the workpaper as the re-performance evidence.
testing.done: each sampled figure is independently reproduced from the cited run and differences are recorded as exceptions.

testing.step: Trace every quoted figure to the submitted regulatory return
actions: Where the answer quotes a reported number, open the submitted QRT for that reference date and locate the cell, for example S.12.01 best estimate or S.22.01 for transitional and matching adjustment effects.
Confirm the answer describes the submitted version and not a later restatement, using the BEEDS receipt and any resubmission history.
Flag any answer that quotes a management figure while implying it is the reported figure.
Record the template code, cell reference and receipt number for each traced figure.
testing.done: each quoted reported figure traces to a template cell in the submitted return with its BEEDS receipt referenced.

testing.step: Test the review and sign-off chain on the sampled responses
actions: Confirm a peer review sheet exists, is initialled, and predates the sign-off date on every sampled response.
Confirm legal clearance is recorded and predates sending for every response containing an error admission or a forward commitment.
Confirm the senior manager signature is present with name and date, and that the signer was the holder of that senior management function on that date.
Treat a response sent before any of these dates as a control failure rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled response shows peer review, legal clearance and senior manager sign-off all dated before sending.

testing.step: Test commitment closure against the wording actually sent
actions: Read the sent responses in the sample and list every forward-looking statement independently of the commitment register.
Match each to a commitment record and check the promised date, the owner and the closure evidence attached.
Re-perform closure on three commitments by inspecting the underlying artefact, such as the changed methodology document or the remediated data field.
Record any commitment closed without evidence, closed late, or never registered as an exception.
testing.done: every promise in the sampled responses maps to a commitment record with evidence, and closures are re-performed on three.

testing.step: Test consistency of answers across the correspondence history
actions: Group the sampled inquiries by subject tag and read the answers on the same subject in date order.
Identify any change in stated methodology, contract boundary treatment or assumption that was not flagged to the PRA as a change.
Check the answers against the most recent SFCR and ORSA text for the same subject and list any contradiction.
Report contradictions to the Chief Actuary for a decision on whether a correction to the PRA is required.
testing.done: answers on the same subject are read in sequence and every unflagged change or contradiction is listed and escalated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the PRA reference, the sub-question affected and the regulatory relationship impact.
Assign a root cause from inquiry not registered, deadline miscomputed, figure not traced to a run, review skipped under time pressure, or commitment not captured.
Set an owner and a remediation date and require the exception to be retested in the next semi-annual cycle.
Escalate any inaccurate answer sent to the PRA to the Chief Risk Officer within two business days for a correction decision.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time acknowledgement rate, the on-time response rate and the figure re-performance exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the reviewer who drafted, reviewed or signed no sampled response sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion, open commitments and any correction issued to the PRA to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with timeliness rates, a stated conclusion and a dated Board Risk Committee reporting reference.

In-scope systems.value: Asset-level holdings, sector and geography exposures and carbon intensity come from the investment platform; narrative and sign-off are assembled in the reporting repository and filed to the PRA through BEEDS

checklist.step: Scope the reporting year against the current PRA survey and SFCR structure
actions: Download the PRA climate data survey template and instructions issued for the reporting year and read the SFCR structure set out in PS3/24 phase 2.
Build the question inventory: one row per survey question and per required SFCR climate statement, with the metric, the unit, the reference date and the required scope.
Compare against last year's inventory and mark every added, removed or reworded question so nothing is answered from memory.
Assign each row a data owner in Investment Operations, Facilities, Underwriting or the actuarial function.
checklist.done: a question inventory exists for the reporting year with every row scoped, unit-defined and owned.

checklist.step: Issue the data request pack to the owning functions
actions: Send each data owner a request naming the exact fields, the reference date of 31 December, the required unit and the return date at reference date plus 25 business days.
Include the definition to be applied for each field, for example enterprise value including cash for financed emissions attribution, so owners do not invent their own basis.
Require each response to state its source system, extraction date and whether any figure is estimated.
Track responses on the inventory and chase any owner two business days after the return date.
checklist.done: every data owner has a dated request with field definitions and every response is tracked to receipt.

checklist.step: Extract the investment holdings position at the reference date
actions: Run the holdings report at 31 December for all portfolios backing the UK Life and Annuities entity, including the matching adjustment portfolio and any pooled fund look-through available.
Extract per holding: issuer name, legal entity identifier, ISIN, asset class, sector classification, country of risk, market value and the portfolio it sits in.
Reconcile total market value to the S.06.02 asset template prepared for the same reference date and explain any difference.
Deliver the file with a control total and flag every holding where look-through is unavailable.
checklist.done: the holdings extract reconciles to S.06.02 market value and flags every position without look-through.

checklist.step: Compute financed emissions and carbon intensity over the investment book
actions: Match each holding to issuer emissions data by legal entity identifier, and record the data vintage and provider for every match.

Compute attributed scope 1 and 2 emissions per holding using the attribution factor of market value divided by issuer enterprise value including cash, and aggregate to weighted average carbon intensity per million of revenue.
Compute the coverage percentage as matched market value over total market value and record it beside every emissions metric.
Where issuer data is missing, apply the documented sector-average proxy, label the result as estimated, and list the affected holdings separately.
checklist.done: financed emissions and weighted average carbon intensity are computed with a stated coverage percentage and every proxy labelled.

checklist.step: Collect the operational emissions and energy data
actions: Collect from Facilities the electricity, gas and district heating consumption for every occupied UK site for the calendar year, in kilowatt hours from supplier invoices.
Collect business travel distance by mode and fleet fuel from the travel provider and expense records, splitting air travel by short and long haul.
Apply the UK Government greenhouse gas conversion factors for the reporting year and record the factor version used against each line.
Produce scope 1, scope 2 location-based and market-based, and the reported scope 3 categories, with the boundary and any excluded site stated.
checklist.done: operational emissions are computed by scope with the conversion factor version, boundary and exclusions stated.

checklist.step: Quantify physical risk exposure across assets and liabilities
actions: Map the property-backed and real-asset holdings to geographic coordinates and run flood, coastal inundation, windstorm and wildfire hazard scoring at the reference date.
Report exposed market value by hazard and by hazard severity band, and name the hazard dataset and version used.
Provide the equivalent geographic concentration for any insured exposure that falls within the survey scope.
Hand the output to the Sustainability Risk Manager with the unmapped share of market value stated explicitly.
checklist.done: exposed market value by hazard and severity band is produced with the dataset version and the unmapped share stated.

checklist.step: Quantify transition risk exposure by sector
actions: Classify every holding to a climate-policy-relevant sector, separating oil and gas, coal, utilities, energy-intensive industry, transport and real estate.
Compute exposure as market value and as a percentage of total invested assets for each sector, at the reference date and at the prior reference date for comparison.
Identify holdings with a stated transition plan or science-based target and report that share separately from the rest.
Record the classification standard used so the same basis can be reproduced next year.
checklist.done: sector exposure is reported in value and percentage terms with a prior-year comparison and a named classification standard.

checklist.step: Assemble the governance and risk management narrative
actions: Document who holds the SS3/19 climate responsibility, evidenced by the Statement of Responsibilities and the Management Responsibilities Map.
Record the board and Risk Committee meetings in the year at which climate risk was discussed, with the minute reference for each.
Describe how climate risk is embedded in the risk appetite statement, the underwriting and investment mandates and the ORSA, citing the approved documents by version.
Confirm each narrative claim against a dated artefact and remove any claim that cannot be evidenced.
checklist.done: each governance statement is backed by a named artefact, minute reference or document version.

checklist.step: Draft the climate sections of the SFCR
actions: Draft the climate content into SFCR section B for governance and section C for risk profile, following the PS3/24 phase 2 structure and headings.
Insert each metric with its unit, coverage percentage, reference date, basis and whether it is measured or estimated, in the same table format each year.
Cross-check every figure against the SFCR quantitative templates and the audited financial statements so no climate figure contradicts a reported figure.
Maintain a reference sheet mapping each disclosed sentence to the evidence file that supports it.
checklist.done: SFCR climate sections are drafted in the PS3/24 structure with every metric labelled and mapped to evidence.

checklist.step: Obtain internal assurance over the disclosed metrics
actions: Independently recompute the weighted average carbon intensity, total attributed emissions and coverage percentage from the holdings and emissions inputs.
Recompute operational scope 1 and 2 emissions from three sample invoices per site and confirm the conversion factor version applied.
Compare your results to the drafted figures and require correction of any difference above 5 per cent before the draft moves on.
Record the assurance notes and the residual differences accepted, with the reason for each acceptance.
checklist.done: each disclosed metric is independently recomputed and differences above 5 per cent are corrected before sign-off.

checklist.step: Complete the PRA climate data survey response
actions: Transfer each assured figure into the PRA survey template against the question number it answers, respecting the template units and rounding rules.
Answer every free-text question with the basis, the scope and the limitations, and never leave a question blank without using the stated not-applicable convention.
Run the template validations and reconcile the survey totals to the SFCR climate tables so the two returns cannot disagree.
Circulate the completed template with the reference sheet to the Chief Risk Officer for review.
checklist.done: every survey question is answered from an assured figure and the survey reconciles to the SFCR climate tables.

checklist.step: Take the disclosure to the Risk Committee and the board for approval
actions: Table the survey response, the SFCR climate sections, the assurance notes and the coverage limitations at the Risk Committee at reference date plus 45 business days.
Present the year-on-year movement in each metric with the driver, separating real portfolio change from data or methodology change.
Take the board approval of the SFCR as a whole and minute the specific approval of the climate content and its stated limitations.
Record the approving meeting date and minute reference on the disclosure reference sheet.
checklist.done: board approval of the climate disclosure is minuted with the movement drivers and limitations presented.

checklist.step: Submit the SFCR and the survey to the PRA inside the deadline
actions: Compute the SFCR deadline as 31 December plus 70 business days for the solo entity and confirm the survey date stated in the PRA request.
Upload the SFCR and its templates to the BEEDS portal under the annual return for the reference year, and the survey to the slot named in the PRA instructions.
Clear any validation error, resubmit and save both submission receipts with reference numbers and timestamps.
Publish the SFCR on the company website on the same day as submission and record the publication URL and date.
checklist.done: both returns show accepted BEEDS receipts before their deadlines and the SFCR publication date and URL are recorded.

checklist.step: Log disclosure exceptions and data gaps for next year
actions: Raise an issue for every coverage gap below 90 per cent, every proxied metric and every question answered with a qualified response.
Assign a root cause such as missing issuer data, no fund look-through, unmetered site or absent travel records, and name the owner who can close it.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next reference date so the gap is closed before the next collection cycle starts.
Report the aggregate coverage position and the open gaps to the Board Risk Committee.
checklist.done: every coverage gap and proxy has an issue with a root cause, an owner and a remediation date before the next reference date.

checklist.step: File the climate disclosure evidence pack
actions: Deposit the question inventory, data request responses, holdings extract, emissions workbook with factor sources, hazard output, assurance notes, board minute and both submission receipts as one indexed pack.
Name the pack by reporting year and apply the 10-year retention label measured from the 31 December reference date.
Confirm the pack is searchable by metric name, survey question number and reference year.
Grant read-only access to Internal Audit and the external assurance provider.
checklist.done: the pack is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by metric and survey question number.

testing.step: Rebuild the disclosure population from the submitted returns
actions: Take the submitted PRA survey and the published SFCR climate sections and list every quantitative metric and every factual assertion as a separate population row.
Compare the row count to the question inventory and treat any question answered in the return but absent from the inventory, or the reverse, as an exception.
Confirm you are testing the submitted version by matching it to the BEEDS receipt and the website publication.
Sign the population as complete and record the source documents in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population covers every submitted metric and assertion and is tied to the BEEDS receipt and published SFCR.

testing.step: Reconcile the holdings base to the source of record
actions: Run your own holdings report at 31 December for the same portfolios and compare position count and total market value to the extract used for the disclosure.
Reconcile the total to the submitted S.06.02 asset template and investigate any difference above 1 per cent of market value.
Check that the matching adjustment portfolio and any pooled funds were included rather than silently dropped.
Record the reconciliation and treat any excluded portfolio not disclosed as an exclusion as an exception.
testing.done: the holdings base reconciles to the investment platform and to S.06.02 with every exclusion disclosed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of metrics and holdings
actions: Take 100 per cent of headline metrics: total attributed emissions, weighted average carbon intensity, coverage percentage, scope 1 and scope 2 operational emissions.
Take 30 holdings by seeded random selection stratified by market value, plus all holdings in the top 20 by attributed emissions.
Take five free-text survey answers by random selection for assertion testing.
Record the seed, strata and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all headline metrics, the largest emitters and a reproducible random selection of holdings and assertions.

testing.step: Recompute the financed emissions calculation independently
actions: Rebuild the attribution for the sampled holdings from market value and issuer enterprise value including cash, using the issuer emissions figure and vintage recorded in the workbook.
Recompute the weighted average carbon intensity over the full matched population and compare to the disclosed figure.
Test the coverage percentage by recomputing matched market value over total market value and comparing to the disclosed coverage.
Record any difference above the 5 per cent threshold as an exception with the driver identified.
testing.done: attributed emissions, carbon intensity and coverage are independently recomputed and differences above 5 per cent are logged.

testing.step: Vouch operational emissions to source invoices and factors
actions: Select two sites and three months each, and agree the kilowatt hour consumption in the workbook to the supplier invoices.
Confirm the conversion factor applied is the UK Government factor for the reporting year and the correct fuel and scope category.
Recompute scope 1 and scope 2 location-based and market-based figures for those sites and extend the error rate to the total.
Check that every occupied site is either included or listed as an excluded site in the disclosed boundary.
testing.done: sampled consumption agrees to invoices, factors are the correct year and category, and every site is included or disclosed as excluded.

testing.step: Test every proxy and estimate for disclosure as such
actions: List every holding where a sector-average proxy replaced issuer data and compute the proxied share of attributed emissions.
Read the disclosed text and confirm the proxy basis and the proxied share are stated, not buried or omitted.
Confirm the proxy methodology in the workbook matches the methodology described in the disclosure.
Treat any unlabelled estimate presented as measured as a fail regardless of its size.
testing.done: every proxy is quantified and disclosed with its basis, and no estimate is presented as a measured figure.

testing.step: Test the governance assertions against the underlying records
actions: Take each sampled free-text governance assertion and open the minute, Statement of Responsibilities or policy version it cites.
Confirm the cited board or Risk Committee meeting actually discussed climate risk by reading the minute rather than the agenda.
Confirm the named senior manager held the climate responsibility on the reference date per the Management Responsibilities Map.
List any assertion with no supporting artefact as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled governance assertion is supported by a minute, responsibilities record or policy version of the right date.

testing.step: Recompute the deadlines and prove submission and publication were timely
actions: Recompute the SFCR deadline as 31 December plus 70 business days on the UK business day calendar and read the survey date from the PRA instruction letter.
Compare both BEEDS receipt timestamps to the recomputed dates and record days early or late.
Confirm the website publication date of the SFCR and that the published version matches the submitted version page for page.
Treat any late submission or any divergence between published and submitted versions as a reportable breach.
testing.done: both deadlines are recomputed and receipts plus publication evidence prove timely, consistent disclosure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the metric or question affected and the difference between disclosed and re-performed values.
Assign a root cause from missing issuer data, wrong conversion factor year, portfolio excluded without disclosure, unevidenced assertion or late submission.
Set an owner and a remediation date before the next reference date and require retest in the next annual cycle.
Escalate any materially misstated public disclosure to the Chief Risk Officer within two business days for a restatement decision.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, quantified difference, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the metric exception rate and compare coverage to the 90 per cent threshold and the re-performance differences to the 5 per cent threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, referencing the workpaper sections that support it.
Have the reviewer who prepared or approved no disclosed metric sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any restatement to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with coverage and exception rates, a stated conclusion and a dated committee reporting reference.

checklist.step: Agree the scenario set with the Board Risk Committee before any modelling
actions: Propose the scenario set for the cycle: an orderly transition to net zero by 2050, a disorderly delayed transition, and a hot house world current policies pathway, plus one firm-specific reverse stress.
State the horizon for each, separating the short-term ORSA business plan horizon of three to five years from the long-term pathway to 2050.
Explain to the committee why each scenario is relevant to an annuity book with long-dated credit assets, and record the challenge and the agreed set in the minute.
Fix the scenario set in writing before calibration begins so the exercise cannot be reshaped around a comfortable answer.
checklist.done: the scenario set, horizons and rationale are agreed and minuted by the Board Risk Committee before calibration.

checklist.step: Calibrate the macro-financial variables from the published scenario source
actions: Download the current NGFS scenario vintage and extract, for each agreed pathway, the carbon price path, GDP path, inflation path and policy rate path for the United Kingdom and the euro area.
Record the vintage, model provider (REMIND, GCAM or MESSAGE), download date and the exact series name for every variable used.
Derive the risk-free curve shift, credit spread widening by rating band and equity and property value shocks consistent with each pathway, documenting the derivation step by step.
Have the calibration workbook reviewed by the Capital Model Actuary before it is loaded into the model.
checklist.done: every scenario variable traces to a named published series and vintage, with derivations documented and reviewed.

checklist.step: Translate the pathways into asset shocks over the actual portfolio
actions: Map each holding in the annuity backing portfolio and the matching adjustment portfolio to a climate-policy-relevant sector and a transition sensitivity band.
Apply the scenario spread widening and downgrade migration to each band and compute the revalued market value and the resulting change in matching adjustment benefit.
Model default and downgrade effects on the fundamental spread so the matching adjustment impact is not understated.
Produce the asset-side result per scenario with the ten largest value movements listed by issuer.
checklist.done: each scenario has a revalued portfolio, a matching adjustment impact and a named list of the largest individual movements.

checklist.step: Assess physical risk effects on real assets and operations
actions: Run the hot house world hazard set over the mapped property and infrastructure holdings and the firm's own occupied sites.
Quantify the change in expected damage and business interruption at the scenario horizon and translate it into a value impact per holding.
State the hazard model version, the return periods used and the share of exposure that could not be geolocated.
Deliver the physical risk impact to the Sustainability Risk Manager for aggregation with the transition results.
checklist.done: physical risk value impacts are produced per scenario with model version, return periods and unmapped exposure stated.

checklist.step: Assess liability-side effects on the annuity and protection book
actions: Define the demographic sensitivity for each scenario, covering mortality and longevity effects from heat stress, air quality and healthcare disruption in the hot house pathway.
Apply the agreed mortality improvement adjustment to the annuitant basis and recompute the best estimate liability under each scenario.
Assess expense inflation under each pathway and apply it to the maintenance expense assumption.
State plainly the evidence base and the uncertainty behind each demographic adjustment rather than presenting it as a precise figure.
checklist.done: each scenario has a recomputed best estimate liability with the demographic and expense adjustments and their evidence base stated.

checklist.step: Project the solvency position through each scenario
actions: Run each scenario through the projection model from the latest reported position and produce own funds, solvency capital requirement and coverage ratio at each projection year end.
Record the run identifier, model version, assumption set and scenario file for every run in the model change log.
Produce the waterfall from the base coverage ratio to each scenario coverage ratio, split into asset value, matching adjustment, liability and capital requirement effects.
Reconcile the base run to the last reported solvency position before presenting any scenario result.
checklist.done: every scenario has a solvency coverage projection with a run identifier, an attribution waterfall and a base run reconciled to the last reported position.

checklist.step: Validate the scenario runs before results are used
actions: Confirm the model version used for each run is validated and approved for scenario use, and reject any run on an unapproved version.
Check the scenario file loaded matches the signed calibration workbook variable by variable.
Run the plausibility checks: monotonicity across scenario severity, sign of each shock, and no unexplained divergence between similar pathways.
Record validation findings and any limitation that must be disclosed in the ORSA chapter.
checklist.done: each run is confirmed on an approved model version with the loaded scenario matching the signed calibration and findings recorded.

checklist.step: Test the results against the risk appetite statement
actions: Compare each scenario coverage ratio against the board-approved solvency risk appetite, the early warning threshold and the capital management policy trigger points.
Identify which scenario and which projection year first breaches each threshold and state the number of years of headroom.
Compare sector concentration under each scenario to the investment mandate limits and record any limit that would be breached.
Summarise the breaches in a single table for the board with the threshold, the scenario and the breach year.
checklist.done: every scenario result is compared to appetite and mandate limits, with the first breach year identified per threshold.

checklist.step: Define and cost the management actions
actions: For each breach, define the specific action: sector exposure reduction, hedging, reinsurance of longevity, capital injection or repricing of new business.
Estimate the lead time, the cost and the solvency benefit of each action, and state who has authority to execute it and under what trigger.
Test whether the action remains executable in the scenario conditions, for example whether a credit portfolio can be sold in a disorderly transition without a fire-sale discount.
Record actions rejected as impractical, with the reason, so the board sees the constrained set and not only the comfortable one.
checklist.done: each breach has costed actions with lead time, trigger, executor and a stated view on executability under scenario conditions.

checklist.step: Assess the effect on the own solvency needs conclusion
actions: Determine whether the climate scenario results change the assessment of overall solvency needs relative to the standard formula solvency capital requirement.
Where the standard formula does not capture the exposure, quantify the additional own solvency need and state the basis for the quantum.
Confirm whether the risk profile deviates significantly from the assumptions underlying the solvency capital requirement calculation, and record the conclusion either way.
Sign the actuarial input to the own solvency needs section with name and date.
checklist.done: a signed conclusion exists on whether climate risk changes own solvency needs, with any additional need quantified.

checklist.step: Draft the climate chapter of the ORSA report
actions: Write the chapter covering scenario selection and rationale, calibration sources and vintage, methodology per risk driver, results, appetite comparison, management actions and limitations.
Include every scenario run, including those with unfavourable results, and state explicitly if any run was excluded and why.
Cross-reference each figure to its run identifier so a supervisor can request the run and reconcile it.
State the model and data limitations plainly, including unmapped exposure, proxy data and the uncertainty in demographic adjustments.
checklist.done: the chapter presents every run with sources, methodology, results, actions and limitations, each cross-referenced to a run identifier.

checklist.step: Put the results to the board for challenge and approval
actions: Circulate the ORSA including the climate chapter to directors at least five business days before the board meeting through the board portal.
Run the session so directors challenge the scenario severity, the demographic assumptions and the executability of management actions, and capture each challenge verbatim.
Minute the board's approval of the ORSA, the specific conclusion on climate risk and any action required before the next cycle.
Record the approval date because it starts the two-week submission clock.
checklist.done: the board challenge is minuted with a dated approval of the ORSA and its climate conclusion.

checklist.step: Submit the ORSA supervisory report to the PRA within two weeks of approval
actions: Compute the submission deadline as board approval date plus two weeks under Conditions Governing Business 3 and post it on the regulatory calendar.
Upload the approved ORSA supervisory report with the climate chapter and its annexes to the BEEDS portal under the ORSA submission slot.
Save the submission receipt with its reference number and timestamp and compare the sent date to the deadline.
Circulate the receipt to the Chief Risk Officer, the Chief Executive Officer and the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: BEEDS shows an accepted ORSA submission with a receipt dated within two weeks of board approval.

checklist.step: Convert board actions and model limitations into tracked items
actions: Raise an action for every board challenge that requires work before the next cycle, with the owner named in the minute and a date inside the cycle.
Raise an issue for every model or data limitation disclosed, such as unmapped property exposure or absent fund look-through, with the remediation owner.
Link each item to the scenario and the run identifier it arose from so the next cycle can prove closure.
Report open items to the Board Risk Committee quarterly until closed.
checklist.done: every board challenge action and disclosed limitation has an owner, a date and a link to its scenario and run.

checklist.step: File the scenario evidence pack
actions: Deposit the agreed scenario specification, calibration workbook with sources and vintage, asset and liability shock files, run outputs, validation report, management action assessment, board minute and BEEDS receipt as one indexed pack.
Name the pack by ORSA cycle year and apply the 10-year retention label measured from the board approval date.
Confirm the pack is searchable by scenario name, run identifier and approval date.
Grant read-only access to Internal Audit, the model risk function and the external auditor.
checklist.done: the pack is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by scenario name and run identifier.

testing.step: Build the population of scenario runs from the model log, not the report
actions: Extract every climate scenario run executed in the cycle from the model run log, including runs later abandoned or superseded.
Compare the list to the scenarios presented in the board pack and the ORSA chapter.
Treat any run that exists in the log but appears nowhere in the board pack or the ORSA as an automatic exception requiring an explanation from the Chief Risk Officer.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction query in the workpaper.
testing.done: every executed run is in the population and any run absent from the board pack or ORSA is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the base run to the last reported solvency position
actions: Take own funds, solvency capital requirement and coverage ratio from the submitted S.23.01 and S.25 templates for the starting reference date.
Compare them to the base run used as the starting point for every scenario projection.
Investigate any difference and confirm it is explained by an approved post-reporting adjustment rather than a different starting balance sheet.
Record the reconciliation as the anchor for all scenario testing.
testing.done: the scenario base run reconciles to the submitted solvency templates with every difference explained.

testing.step: Draw the sample of scenarios and variables
actions: Take 100 per cent of scenarios that produced an appetite breach and 100 per cent of the reverse stress scenario.
Take 15 calibration variables by seeded random selection across the remaining scenarios, weighted toward the largest solvency impacts.
Take the ten largest individual asset movements per scenario for detailed trace.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all breach and reverse stress scenarios plus a reproducible selection of variables and asset movements.

testing.step: Trace calibration variables back to the published scenario source
actions: For each sampled variable, open the NGFS scenario release of the recorded vintage and locate the named series for the recorded region and pathway.
Compare the published value to the value in the calibration workbook at each projection year used.
Re-derive one credit spread and one equity shock from the published pathway using the documented derivation and compare to the workbook.
Treat any variable with no traceable source, or a vintage different from the one disclosed, as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled variable traces to a named published series and vintage and two derivations are independently reproduced.

testing.step: Re-perform the solvency projection for the most severe scenario
actions: Rebuild the disorderly transition run from the base position using the signed calibration file, without reading the reported result first.
Compare your own funds, solvency capital requirement and coverage ratio at each projection year to the reported figures.
Rebuild the attribution waterfall and check each component sums to the total movement rather than being balanced by a residual.
Record any coverage ratio difference above 2 percentage points as an exception with its driver identified.
testing.done: the most severe scenario is independently re-run and differences above 2 percentage points of coverage are logged with drivers.

testing.step: Test model version control and validation status on every run
actions: For each run in the population, read the model version from the run log and check its validation status and approval date in the model inventory.
Confirm no run used a version whose validation was pending, expired or conditional on unmet actions.
Confirm the scenario file loaded is byte-identical to the signed calibration file by comparing checksums or, failing that, variable by variable.
Treat a run on an unvalidated version as a fail regardless of whether the result was favourable.
testing.done: every run is confirmed on a validated, approved model version with the signed scenario file verifiably loaded.

testing.step: Trace sampled asset movements to holdings and sector classifications
actions: Open each sampled largest movement and confirm the holding, market value and rating at the starting reference date against the investment platform.
Confirm the assigned climate sector and transition sensitivity band match the documented classification standard.
Recompute the shocked value from the applied spread widening and downgrade migration and compare to the model output.
Flag any holding shocked under a sector it does not belong to, since misclassification quietly changes the whole result.
testing.done: each sampled asset movement traces to a real holding with a correct classification and an independently recomputed shocked value.

testing.step: Test that results actually reached the board and the ORSA unchanged
actions: Compare the coverage ratios and breach years in the board pack to the model outputs figure by figure.
Read the board minute and confirm the challenge was recorded and that the climate conclusion was approved rather than merely noted.
Compare the ORSA chapter figures to the board pack figures and identify any change made after board approval.
Treat any post-approval change to a reported figure without a documented board or committee decision as an exception.
testing.done: board pack, minute and ORSA figures agree, and any post-approval change carries a documented decision.

testing.step: Recompute the submission deadline and log exceptions
actions: Recompute the ORSA submission deadline as board approval date plus two weeks and compare it to the BEEDS receipt timestamp.
Raise an issue per exception with the scenario, run identifier, the difference found and the effect on the reported conclusion.
Assign a root cause from unsourced calibration, unvalidated model version, misclassified holdings, run omitted from reporting, or late submission, with an owner and a remediation date.
Escalate any omitted scenario or materially misstated coverage ratio to the Chief Risk Officer within two business days.
testing.done: the deadline is recomputed against the receipt and every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate across sampled variables, runs and asset movements against the 2 percentage point and zero-omission thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the reviewer who built or ran no tested scenario sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion, omitted runs and validation failures to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the model governance repository and the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with exception rates, a stated conclusion and a dated Board Risk Committee reporting reference.
