checklist.step: Maintain the governance map of every body the regime requires
actions: Hold a single governance map listing the board, Audit Committee, Board Risk Committee, Remuneration Committee and Nomination Committee, with the terms of reference version and approval date for each.
Add the four key functions required by Conditions Governing Business 4 to 6 plus risk management, showing the holder, the reporting line and the committee each reports to.
Show for each body its delegated authority, its reserved matters and where those are recorded in the board's schedule of matters reserved.
Reissue the map to directors whenever any element changes rather than at the annual review only.
checklist.done: a current governance map lists every body and key function with terms of reference version, holder and reporting line.

checklist.step: Review and re-approve each committee's terms of reference annually
actions: Sixty days before the anniversary, mark up each terms of reference against Conditions Governing Business 2 to 6, the current prescribed responsibility allocation and any PRA policy statement issued in the year.
Confirm the terms of reference state composition, independence requirement, quorum, frequency, standing agenda items and the right to obtain external advice.
Route the marked-up version to the committee chair for comment, then to the committee and the board for approval.
Publish the approved version to the board portal with a new version number and archive the superseded version without deleting it.
checklist.done: each committee has a dated, board-approved terms of reference for the year with the superseded version archived.

checklist.step: Test committee composition and independence at every change
actions: Maintain a membership register showing for each member the appointment date, role, executive or non-executive status and independence determination with the reasons.
Test each committee against its terms of reference composition rule, including the requirement that the Audit Committee is composed of non-executives with recent and relevant financial experience.
Reassess independence on any change of circumstance such as tenure passing nine years, a related-party relationship or a new external appointment.
Escalate any composition breach to the Nomination Committee chair the day it arises with a proposed remedy and date.
checklist.done: the membership register is current and each committee meets its composition and independence rule or has an escalated remedy.

checklist.step: Build the annual forward agenda so mandatory items cannot be missed
actions: Build a forward agenda per body scheduling every item its terms of reference and the PRA Rulebook require: ORSA approval, SFCR approval, technical provisions review, actuarial function report, internal audit plan and opinion, compliance function report, risk appetite review and policy approvals.
Assign each item an owner, a target meeting and a paper deadline five business days before the meeting.
Track coverage during the year and reschedule any deferred item immediately rather than leaving it to the year-end sweep.
Report forward agenda coverage to each committee chair quarterly.
checklist.done: each body has a forward agenda covering every mandatory item, with owners, target meetings and tracked coverage.

checklist.step: Appoint and record the key function holders
actions: Confirm a named holder for the risk management, compliance, internal audit and actuarial functions, each with a documented appointment approved by the board or the relevant committee.
Confirm each holder has the authority, resources and unrestricted access to information the function needs, and record the headcount and budget agreed for each function.
Confirm the reporting lines preserve independence: internal audit reports to the Audit Committee chair, risk and compliance report to the Board Risk Committee.
Where a role is vacant, appoint an interim holder within 30 days, record the arrangement and notify the PRA where the role is a senior management function.
checklist.done: every key function has a named holder or notified interim, with board-approved authority, resources and an independent reporting line.

checklist.step: Keep the Management Responsibilities Map and Statements of Responsibilities current
actions: Maintain the Management Responsibilities Map showing every senior management function, the prescribed responsibilities allocated and the reporting lines, as a single document covering the whole firm.
Update the map and the affected Statements of Responsibilities on every appointment, departure or reallocation, and have each senior manager sign their statement.
Confirm each prescribed responsibility is allocated to exactly one senior manager with no gap and no unintended duplication.
Submit Form C for a departing senior manager or Form D for a change of details on the FCA and PRA Connect portal within 7 business days of the change.
checklist.done: the responsibilities map and every statement are current and signed, with PRA notifications made within 7 business days.

checklist.step: Run each meeting to the quorum and conflicts rules
actions: Check the quorum against the terms of reference before the meeting opens and record attendees, apologies and those attending by invitation in the attendance register.
Take conflicts of interest declarations at the top of every meeting, record each declaration and record any member who withdrew from an item.
Where quorum is not met, do not take decisions; adjourn and reconvene, and record the adjournment.
Log attendance percentage per member and report it to the Nomination Committee for the effectiveness review.
checklist.done: every meeting has a recorded quorum check, an attendance register and recorded conflicts declarations.

checklist.step: Produce minutes that evidence challenge and decision
actions: Draft minutes within ten business days recording the papers considered, the challenge raised by name, the decision taken, the dissent if any and the actions with owners and dates.
Record explicitly every approval the PRA expects the board to give, naming the document and its version, so approval can be evidenced later.
Circulate the draft to the chair, then to members, and approve at the following meeting with any amendment recorded.
File the signed minute and the papers pack together so a supervisor can read the decision against the evidence it was based on.
checklist.done: each meeting has a signed minute naming challenge, decisions with document versions, and actions with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Track committee actions to closure
actions: Transfer every minuted action into the action log with the committee, the owner, the due date and the evidence required to close it.
Report the open action list at the top of every meeting showing overdue items and days overdue.
Close actions only against the named evidence, never on a verbal confirmation at the meeting.
Escalate any action overdue by two meeting cycles to the committee chair and the Chief Executive Officer.
checklist.done: every minuted action is logged, reported each meeting and closed only against named evidence.

checklist.step: Confirm the key functions have unrestricted access and are being heard
actions: Hold at least two private sessions a year between the Audit Committee and the internal audit function without executives present, and minute that they occurred.
Confirm the same private access arrangements exist between the Board Risk Committee and the risk and compliance functions and between the board and the actuarial function.
Record any instance where a function was denied information, resource or access and report it to the committee chair immediately.
Confirm each function reported to its committee at the frequency its terms of reference require.
checklist.done: private sessions and function reporting occurred at the required frequency with any access restriction escalated.

checklist.step: Run the annual board and committee effectiveness review
actions: Run the annual effectiveness questionnaire covering composition, skills, information quality, time allocated to risk and challenge culture, with an externally facilitated review at least every three years.
Include specific questions on whether directors receive sufficient information on solvency, technical provisions and climate risk to challenge management.
Produce findings with owners and dates and put them to the Nomination Committee and the board for approval.
Track the actions through the governance action log until closed and report progress at the following year's review.
checklist.done: an effectiveness review is completed with findings, owners, dates and board approval, external at least every three years.

checklist.step: Maintain the skills matrix and induction for directors
actions: Maintain a skills matrix mapping each director against actuarial, investment, insurance underwriting, financial reporting, technology and conduct competencies.
Identify gaps and feed them to the Nomination Committee for the succession plan and the recruitment brief.
Deliver induction for every new director covering the Solvency UK framework, the firm's risk profile, the ORSA and the responsibilities regime, and record completion.
Deliver annual continuing development on regulatory change and record attendance per director.
checklist.done: a current skills matrix, a recorded induction per new director and recorded annual development exist.

checklist.step: Review the governance structure against regulatory change
actions: Track PRA and FCA policy statements, supervisory statements and Dear CEO letters through the regulatory change log and assess each for a governance structure impact.
Where an impact exists, raise a change item naming the affected terms of reference, prescribed responsibility or key function, with an owner and an implementation date.
Report the assessment to the Board Risk Committee so the board sees regulatory change before it lands rather than after.
Update the governance map and the affected documents on implementation and record the version change.
checklist.done: each relevant regulatory change has a governance impact assessment, an owner and a recorded document update.

checklist.step: Report the governance position to the board annually
actions: Produce an annual governance report covering terms of reference currency, composition and independence, attendance, agenda coverage, key function continuity, action closure and effectiveness review outcomes.
Show every exception raised in the year with its disposition so the board sees the gaps and not only the compliance rate.
Use the same content to support the System of Governance section of the SFCR so the public disclosure and the internal record cannot diverge.
Obtain board approval of the report and record the minute reference.
checklist.done: a board-approved annual governance report exists covering currency, composition, coverage, continuity and exceptions.

checklist.step: File the governance record under the retention rule
actions: Deposit each year's terms of reference versions, membership and independence records, attendance registers, agendas, papers, signed minutes, action log extract, effectiveness review and responsibilities map history.
Apply the 10-year retention label measured from the date each document was superseded, so version history survives.
Confirm the record is searchable by committee, meeting date, document version and senior management function.
Grant read-only access to Internal Audit, the key function holders and the external auditor.
checklist.done: the governance record is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by committee, date and version.

testing.step: Build the population of meetings and bodies independently
actions: Extract every board and committee meeting held in the half-year from the board portal calendar and the minute library, including adjourned and written-resolution decisions.
Compare the count to the frequency each terms of reference requires and list any body that met fewer times than required.
Add every written resolution and out-of-committee approval so decisions taken outside meetings are in scope.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction method in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population covers every meeting and written resolution and is compared to the required meeting frequency.

testing.step: Reconcile the governance map to the constitutional and regulatory record
actions: Compare the governance map to the Management Responsibilities Map, the articles of association and the Financial Services Register entry for the firm.
Confirm every senior management function shown on the Register is on the map with the same holder, and investigate any name on one and not the other.
Confirm every prescribed responsibility is allocated once, with no gap and no unexplained duplication.
Record any inconsistency as an exception requiring a Form D correction or a map update.
testing.done: the map reconciles to the responsibilities map, the articles and the Financial Services Register with inconsistencies listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of meetings and members
actions: Take 100 per cent of meetings at which a mandatory approval was recorded, such as the ORSA, SFCR, technical provisions or the internal audit plan.
Take 12 further meetings by seeded random selection across bodies from the remaining population.
Take 100 per cent of members whose independence determination changed in the period plus five further members at random.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers every mandatory-approval meeting plus a reproducible random selection of meetings and members.

testing.step: Re-perform the quorum test on every sampled meeting
actions: Read the quorum rule in the terms of reference version in force on the meeting date, not the current version.
Count attendees from the attendance register, excluding those attending by invitation and those who withdrew for the item under a conflict.
Confirm quorum held at the point each decision was taken, not merely at the opening of the meeting.
Treat any decision taken while inquorate as a fail and identify what was decided.
testing.done: quorum is re-tested against the version in force at the decision point for every sampled meeting.

testing.step: Test agenda coverage of every mandatory item across the year
actions: Build a coverage matrix of every item the terms of reference and the PRA Rulebook require against the meetings at which it was actually taken.
Evidence each covered item by the paper reference and the minute paragraph, not by its presence on an agenda.
List items deferred more than once and items not covered at all in the year.
Treat any mandatory item with no minuted coverage in the year as a fail.
testing.done: a coverage matrix evidences every mandatory item by paper and minute reference or lists it as not covered.

testing.step: Test key function holder continuity and independence
actions: Build a timeline for each of the four key functions showing holder, start date, end date and any gap, drawn from the HR record rather than the governance map.
Test any gap against the 30-day interim appointment standard and check whether a PRA notification was required and made.
Confirm the reporting line in the HR record matches the independent line stated in the terms of reference, and flag any function reporting through the executive it must challenge.
Confirm at least two minuted private sessions occurred for internal audit in the year.
testing.done: a continuity timeline per key function exists, gaps are tested against the 30-day standard and reporting lines are confirmed independent.

testing.step: Test independence determinations on sampled members
actions: Read the independence determination for each sampled member and the reasons recorded.
Test tenure against the nine-year threshold, and test for related-party relationships, material business relationships and cross-directorships using the register of interests.
Confirm the Audit Committee members meet the recent and relevant financial experience requirement with the evidence recorded.
List any determination that is stale, unsupported or contradicted by the register of interests.
testing.done: each sampled independence determination is re-tested against tenure, interests and experience evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the senior manager notification deadlines
actions: List every senior manager appointment, departure and change of responsibilities in the period from the HR record and the responsibilities map history.
Recompute the 7 business day notification deadline for each Form C and Form D from the effective date of the change.
Match each to the Connect portal submission confirmation and compare the submission date to the recomputed deadline.
Treat any unnotified or late-notified change as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every senior manager change is matched to a Connect submission and tested against the recomputed 7 business day deadline.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the body, the meeting date or the function affected and the governance consequence.
Assign a root cause from stale terms of reference, agenda item deferred without reschedule, quorum not checked at the decision point, vacancy unmanaged, or notification missed.
Set an owner and a remediation date and require a retest at the next semi-annual cycle.
Escalate any inquorate decision or unnotified senior manager change to the Chief Executive Officer and General Counsel within two business days.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate across meetings, coverage items, members and notifications against the zero-tolerance thresholds for inquorate decisions and uncovered mandatory items.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the reviewer who drafted no tested terms of reference, agenda or minute sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any breach to the Audit Committee and the board and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with exception rates, a stated conclusion and a dated Audit Committee reporting reference.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any filing made after its deadline, any change identified but not filed, and any filed statement later found inconsistent with the governance record is logged with the form name, jurisdiction and days late

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The General Counsel signs off every late filing, every corrective filing and the notification to the regulator or registrar that accompanies it

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every governance filing due in the year across the UK entity and the group, plus every triggering event in the period taken from board minutes, HR records and the register of directors, whether or not a filing was made

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed statutory deadlines: any filing after its due date is a fail; any triggering event with no filing is a fail; any filed statement contradicting the governance record is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Filings are annual and event-driven, so the test runs semi-annually over all filings due and all triggering events in the half-year, with the annual cycle covering the SFCR and Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure in full

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside the company secretariat and legal function and must not have prepared, reviewed or signed any tested filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual governance filing test workpaper (filing inventory, trigger event population, deadline recomputation, content trace to source records, receipt verification, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filing register with due dates, submission dates, receipts and the filed documents themselves, producible to the PRA, Companies House or a US lead state examiner within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Corporate Secretary responds to registrar and supervisory queries on filings with General Counsel clearance; corrective filings are approved by the General Counsel before submission and reported to the board

checklist.step: Maintain the governance filing inventory across every jurisdiction
actions: Hold one row per filing obligation: form name, jurisdiction, regulator or registrar, legal entity, trigger (annual or event), due-date rule, signatory and submission channel.

Cover the SFCR System of Governance section to the PRA, Companies House CS01, AP01, TM01, CH01 and persons of significant control forms, Connect Form C and Form D, and the group Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure, Form B and Form F.
Confirm each due-date rule against the current statute or rulebook text at least annually and record the date checked.
Reissue the inventory to the legal and secretariat team whenever an entity is added, dissolved or redomiciled.
checklist.done: the inventory lists every governance filing with jurisdiction, trigger, due-date rule, signatory and a dated rule check.

checklist.step: Detect triggering events the day they occur
actions: Take a daily feed of director and senior manager joiners, leavers and role changes from the HR record and the board minute actions.
Add changes in registered office, share capital, articles, persons of significant control and group ownership from legal and finance.
Match each event to the filing inventory rows it triggers and open a filing task with the computed due date the same day.
Escalate any event discovered more than five days after it occurred so the shortened remaining window is visible immediately.
checklist.done: every governance event is captured the day it occurs and matched to its triggered filings with a computed due date.

checklist.step: Assemble the SFCR System of Governance content from the governance record
actions: Draft SFCR section B in the PS3/24 phase 2 structure covering board and committee structure, key functions, fit and proper policy, risk management system including the ORSA, internal control, internal audit, actuarial function, outsourcing and adequacy assessment.
Source every statement from the governance map, terms of reference versions, key function holder register and board minutes, and record the source against each paragraph.
Include the remuneration policy disclosure and any material outsourcing arrangement with the service provider and jurisdiction named.
Cross-check the narrative against the audited financial statements and the ORSA so the same facts are stated the same way.
checklist.done: SFCR section B is drafted in the required structure with every statement mapped to a governance record source.

checklist.step: Prepare the Companies House statutory filings
actions: For the confirmation statement, verify the registered office, registered email address, SIC codes, statement of capital, shareholder list and persons of significant control against the statutory registers before completing CS01.
For director changes, prepare AP01 with full name, date of birth, nationality, occupation, service address and residential address, or TM01 with the termination date exactly as minuted.
Reconcile the statutory registers to the board minutes so the filing reports the date of the decision, not the date it was noticed.
Have the Corporate Secretary check each form against the source register entry before it is submitted.
checklist.done: each Companies House form is completed from verified statutory register entries reconciled to the board minute.

checklist.step: Prepare the Connect notifications for senior managers and Directory persons
actions: For a departing senior manager, complete Form C stating the cessation date, the reason for cessation and whether any concern about fitness and propriety arose.
For a change of responsibilities or details, complete Form D and attach the revised Statement of Responsibilities and the updated Management Responsibilities Map.
For certified and non-senior-manager Directory persons, update the Directory record with the role, start or end date and the customer-facing status.
Have the General Counsel review any Form C that records a concern before it is submitted, because it drives regulatory references.
checklist.done: each Form C, Form D and Directory update is completed with the correct dates, attachments and legal review where a concern is recorded.

checklist.step: Prepare the group Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure
actions: Confirm the lead state for the insurance holding company system and the level at which the disclosure is filed (ultimate controlling person, intermediate holding company or insurer).

Draft the disclosure covering board structure and committee composition, director qualification and election process, board and management oversight of critical risk areas, and executive compensation and succession planning.
State whether the governance framework has changed since the prior filing and describe each change rather than refiling identical text.
Route to the General Counsel for the confidentiality treatment note and to the signing officer for execution.
checklist.done: the disclosure is drafted at the correct filing level, describes changes since the prior year and is cleared for signature.

checklist.step: Prepare the holding company registration and enterprise risk forms
actions: Complete the Form B registration statement with the current organisational chart, the ultimate controlling person, all affiliated agreements and any change since the last filing.
Complete the Form F enterprise risk report identifying material risks in the holding company system that could pose enterprise risk to the insurer.
Reconcile the organisational chart to the legal entity register and the group structure used in the SFCR so the two disclosures agree.
Confirm the lead state due dates and the filing method for each form before assembling the submission.
checklist.done: Form B and Form F are complete, reconciled to the legal entity register and matched to the lead state due dates.

checklist.step: Legal review every filing before it leaves the building
actions: Read each filing for factual accuracy against the source records, for consistency with the prior year filing and for any statement that creates a commitment.
Confirm the confidentiality treatment claimed for the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure is stated correctly for the lead state.
Confirm the signatory holds the authority to sign under the board delegation or the articles and that the delegation is current.
Record the clearance with date on the filing task and hold any filing where a source record is missing.
checklist.done: each filing carries a dated legal clearance confirming accuracy, consistency and signatory authority.

checklist.step: Obtain board or authorised signatory approval
actions: Take the SFCR, including section B, to the board for approval and record the approval in the minute with the document version.
Take the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure for board or authorised officer signature depending on the filing level, and record who signed and on what authority.
For routine Companies House and Connect filings, confirm the standing delegation to the Corporate Secretary covers the form and is unexpired.
Record the approval reference on the filing task before submission.
checklist.done: each filing has a recorded approval or a valid standing delegation, referenced on the filing task.

checklist.step: Submit each filing through its own portal and capture the receipt
actions: Submit the SFCR to the PRA through BEEDS under the annual return slot and save the receipt with reference number and timestamp.
Submit Companies House forms through WebFiling using the company authentication code and save the acceptance email and the updated public record entry.
Submit Form C, Form D and Directory updates through the FCA and PRA Connect portal and save the submission confirmation.
Lodge the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure, Form B and Form F with the lead state by the prescribed method and save the acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every filing has a saved receipt or acknowledgement showing the regulator or registrar accepted it.

checklist.step: Verify the public record reflects what was filed
actions: Three business days after each Companies House submission, open the company's public filing history and confirm the document appears with the correct date and content.
Check the Financial Services Register and the PRA Directory to confirm senior manager and certified person changes are reflected.
Where the public record is wrong, prepare the corrective filing immediately rather than waiting for the next cycle.
Record the verification date and outcome on the filing task.
checklist.done: each submission is verified on the public record within three business days with corrections raised immediately.

checklist.step: Publish the SFCR and record the publication
actions: Publish the approved SFCR on the company website on the day of submission, in the location the PRA disclosure rules require it to remain accessible.
Confirm the published file is identical to the submitted version and record the file hash or version reference.
Keep prior years accessible for the period the disclosure rules require and record the retention arrangement.
Record the publication date and URL on the filing task and notify the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: the SFCR is published on the day of submission, identical to the submitted version, with the date and URL recorded.

checklist.step: Log late or missed filings and file the correction
actions: Raise an issue the moment a filing passes its due date, recording the form, jurisdiction, days late and the cause.
Prepare the late filing immediately and, where the registrar or regulator expects notification of the lateness, send it with General Counsel clearance.
Assess whether a penalty or a public record consequence applies and record the assessment and any amount paid.
Report every late filing to the board at its next meeting rather than absorbing it in an aggregate compliance rate.
checklist.done: each late or missed filing has an issue with days late, the correction filed and board reporting.

checklist.step: Report the filing position to the board annually
actions: Produce an annual filing report showing every obligation, its due date, its filing date, the receipt reference and any exception.
Show the trigger events in the year and confirm each produced the filings it should have.
Present the changes described in the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure and confirm they match the governance changes the board actually made.
Obtain board acknowledgement and record the minute reference.
checklist.done: a board-acknowledged annual filing report exists covering obligations, filing dates, receipts and exceptions.

checklist.step: File the filing evidence pack under the retention rule
actions: Deposit each filed document, its source records, legal clearance, approval reference, submission receipt and public record verification as one indexed pack per filing.
Apply the 10-year retention label measured from the filing date and name the pack by entity, form and period.
Confirm the pack is searchable by form name, jurisdiction, entity and filing date.
Grant read-only access to Internal Audit and the external auditor.
checklist.done: each filing pack is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by form, jurisdiction and date.

testing.step: Build the population of obligations and triggering events independently
actions: Extract all director and senior manager joiners, leavers and role changes in the period from the HR record and the register of directors, without using the filing tracker.
Add registered office, share capital, articles and ownership changes from the board minutes and the legal entity register.
List every annual obligation due in the period from the statutory rules rather than from the inventory, then reconcile to the inventory.
Treat any event or obligation absent from the filing tracker as an automatic exception and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: an independently built population of events and annual obligations is reconciled to the tracker with gaps listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed record to the public register
actions: Open the Companies House filing history for the entity and list every document filed in the period with its date.
Compare it to the filing tracker and to your event population, in both directions, so both unfiled events and unexpected filings surface.
Check the Financial Services Register and the PRA Directory entries against the senior manager and certified person population.
Record any difference between the public record and the internal record as an exception.
testing.done: the public register, the filing tracker and the event population are reconciled in both directions.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of filings
actions: Take 100 per cent of annual filings: the SFCR, the confirmation statement, the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure, Form B and Form F.
Take 100 per cent of filings recorded as late and 100 per cent of Form C filings that recorded a fitness concern.
Take 15 event-driven filings by seeded random selection from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers every annual filing, every late filing and a reproducible selection of event-driven filings.

testing.step: Recompute every deadline from the statutory rule
actions: Recompute the SFCR deadline as 31 December plus 70 business days, the confirmation statement as review period end plus 14 days, director changes as change date plus 14 days and Form C and Form D as change date plus 7 business days.
Recompute the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure as the lead state 1 June date and Form F as the lead state prescribed date.
Compare each recomputed deadline to the receipt timestamp and record days early or late.
Treat any filing after its statutory deadline as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled deadline is recomputed from the statutory rule and compared to its receipt timestamp.

testing.step: Trace filed content back to the source governance records
actions: For sampled Companies House forms, agree names, dates of birth, appointment or termination dates and addresses to the statutory register and the board minute.
For the SFCR section B, select ten statements and agree each to the governance map, terms of reference version or minute cited.
For the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure, agree the described board and committee structure to the terms of reference in force at the filing date.
Record any filed statement that the governance record does not support as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled filed fact traces to a statutory register entry, minute or governance document of the right date.

testing.step: Test consistency across filings made in different jurisdictions
actions: Compare the group organisational chart in Form B to the group structure described in the SFCR and to the legal entity register.
Compare the board and committee composition in the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure to the composition disclosed in SFCR section B at the same date.
Compare the named senior managers on the Financial Services Register to those described in the SFCR governance narrative.
List every inconsistency with the two documents and the specific contradictory statements quoted.
testing.done: structures and compositions are compared across all governance filings and each contradiction is quoted and listed.

testing.step: Verify approval and signatory authority on each sampled filing
actions: Confirm the board minute approving the SFCR names the version filed and predates the submission date.
Confirm the person who signed each filing held the delegated authority on the signing date, by reading the board delegation or the articles.
Confirm legal clearance is recorded and predates submission for every sampled filing.
Treat a filing submitted before approval or signed without current authority as a control failure.
testing.done: every sampled filing shows approval, valid signatory authority and legal clearance all dated before submission.

testing.step: Verify receipts and public record confirmation
actions: Open the saved receipt for each sampled filing and confirm the reference number, entity, form and timestamp match the tracker entry.
For the SFCR, confirm the published website version is identical to the submitted version and that the publication date matches the submission date.
For Companies House filings, confirm the document appears on the public filing history with the expected content.
Record any filing with no receipt, a mismatched receipt or an unverified public record as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled filing has a matched receipt and, where public, a verified public record entry.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the form, jurisdiction, entity, days late or the unsupported statement.
Assign a root cause from event not detected, deadline miscomputed, source record not verified, approval obtained after filing, or receipt not captured.
Set an owner and a remediation date and require the exception to be retested in the next semi-annual cycle.
Escalate any unfiled statutory obligation to the General Counsel within one business day so the corrective filing starts immediately.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the content accuracy exception rate against the zero-tolerance deadline threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the reviewer who prepared or signed no tested filing sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion, every late filing and every corrective filing to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with on-time and accuracy rates, a stated conclusion and a dated Audit Committee reporting reference.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the fitness and propriety assessment process for directors, senior management function holders and key function holders; the General Counsel owns the regulatory approval applications and the Chief Executive Officer holds the prescribed responsibility for the firm's fitness and propriety arrangements

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Insurance – Fitness and Propriety 2 (assessment), 3 (notification) and 4 (records), read with the Insurance Fitness and Propriety regulatory reference requirement to obtain references covering the previous six years and the PRA and FCA Connect application forms in force at the assessment date

In-scope processes.value: Per-appointment and annual fitness and propriety assessment for every director, senior management function holder, key function holder and certified person of the UK Life and Annuities entity, plus reassessment on any change of circumstance

In-scope systems.value: Candidate and employee records, assessment outcomes and certification status are held in the HR system; approvals and notifications are filed on the FCA and PRA Connect portal and screening results come from the background screening providers

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fitness and Propriety Assessment Procedure — role classification, competence evidence, honesty and integrity screening, financial soundness check, regulatory references for six years, interview and challenge, decision record, Form A submission and annual recertification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Nomination Committee on the recommendation of the Chief HR Officer and the General Counsel; reviewed annually and re-approved on any change to the Connect forms, the reference template or the certification population

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form A must be approved before the individual performs a senior management function; regulatory references must be provided to a requesting firm within six weeks of request; Form C on cessation and Form D on change of details within 7 business days; certification renewed annually before the certificate expiry date

Deadline reminders configured.value: The HR system raises tasks at offer acceptance for the assessment start, at reference request plus 10 and plus 25 business days for chasing, at certificate expiry minus 60 and minus 30 days for recertification, and on the day of any leaver record for the 7 business day Form C clock

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Assessment record, criminal record and credit check results, regulatory references received and given, interview notes, decision rationale and the Connect submission retained 6 years after the individual ceases the role, and 10 years for senior management functions

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any individual performing a senior management function before approval, any missing reference year in the six-year period, any lapsed certificate and any late Form C is logged with the individual and the role named

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The General Counsel signs off every assessment where an adverse finding was disclosed, every decision to certify despite a concern, and every notification to the PRA arising from a fitness and propriety failure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every appointment, reappointment, annual certification and cessation of a director, senior management function holder, key function holder or certified person in the period, taken from the HR record and the Financial Services Register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance: any individual who performed a senior management function before Connect approval is a fail; any assessment missing a required screening element or a year of the six-year reference period is a fail; any certificate renewed after expiry is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per appointment and annually thereafter, so the test runs semi-annually over all appointments and cessations in the half-year plus a full annual sweep of the certification population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside HR and the legal function and must not have conducted or approved any tested assessment

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual fitness and propriety test workpaper (appointment population, Register reconciliation, assessment file inspection, reference coverage analysis, approval date comparison, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository with restricted access for personal data

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Assessment records, screening evidence, references and Connect submissions per individual, producible to the PRA or FCA within 5 business days under Fitness and Propriety 4 record-keeping

Regulator response path.value: The General Counsel leads any PRA or FCA enquiry into an individual's fitness and propriety; the Chief HR Officer provides the assessment file and the Data Protection Officer clears the disclosure of personal data

checklist.step: Classify the role before the search starts
actions: Determine with the General Counsel whether the role is a senior management function requiring pre-approval, a key function holder role, a certified role or none of these.
Record the specific function reference, for example SMF1 chief executive, SMF2 chief finance, SMF4 chief risk or SMF20 chief actuary, on the requisition.
Write the competence requirement for the role in evidence terms: qualifications, years of relevant experience, regulatory experience and the specific technical competence the function needs.
Confirm which prescribed responsibilities the role will hold so the Statement of Responsibilities can be drafted alongside the assessment.
checklist.done: the role carries a recorded regulatory classification, function reference, competence requirement and intended responsibilities.

checklist.step: Collect the candidate's declaration and full history
actions: Issue the fitness and propriety questionnaire covering criminal convictions, regulatory investigations, disciplinary findings, directorship disqualifications, insolvency, county court judgments and dismissal for misconduct.
Require a complete employment history for the previous six years with no unexplained gaps, and require a written explanation for every gap over one month.
Collect qualification certificates, professional body membership evidence and continuing professional development records.
Obtain the candidate's written consent for criminal record, credit and reference checks and record the consent date.
checklist.done: a signed declaration, a gap-free six-year history, qualification evidence and dated consents are on file.

checklist.step: Run the honesty and integrity screening
actions: Order the criminal records check appropriate to the role and confirm the certificate is dated within three months of the appointment decision.
Screen the candidate against sanctions lists, politically exposed person lists and adverse media, and record the screening date, provider and result.
Check the Financial Services Register and the FCA and PRA enforcement notices for the candidate's name and any firm they held a controlled function at.
Check the Companies House disqualified directors register and the insolvency register and record each result, including nil results.
checklist.done: criminal record, sanctions, adverse media, enforcement, disqualification and insolvency checks are recorded with dates and results.

checklist.step: Assess financial soundness
actions: Order the credit check and record county court judgments, defaults, bankruptcy orders, individual voluntary arrangements and debt relief orders with dates and amounts.
Where an adverse entry exists, obtain the candidate's written explanation and the current status of the debt or order.
Assess whether the entry bears on the individual's ability to perform the role honestly, and record the reasoning rather than a pass or fail alone.
Route any adverse finding to the General Counsel before the assessment is concluded.
checklist.done: a dated credit check exists with every adverse entry explained, assessed in writing and escalated where adverse.

checklist.step: Obtain regulatory references covering the full six-year period
actions: Identify every employer in the previous six years from the declared history and request a regulatory reference from each regulated firm using the prescribed template.
Ask specifically for disciplinary findings, breaches of individual conduct rules, fitness and propriety conclusions and the reason for leaving.
Chase at 10 and 25 business days and record every chase; where a firm no longer exists, document the evidence of that and the alternative verification obtained.
Map the references received onto a six-year timeline and identify any period not covered by a reference.
checklist.done: references cover every regulated employment in the six-year period, with gaps documented and alternatives evidenced.

checklist.step: Interview against the competence requirement and record the evidence
actions: Run a structured interview panel including a non-executive director for senior management function roles, using questions mapped to the recorded competence requirement.
Test technical competence specific to the function, for example Solvency UK capital and technical provisions knowledge for a chief actuary or chief finance appointment.
Record the evidence given for each competence, not just a score, and record any competence the panel judged not evidenced.
Where a competence gap exists, define the development plan and the supervision arrangement before the appointment proceeds.
checklist.done: a structured interview record exists mapping evidence to each competence, with gaps and development plans stated.

checklist.step: Reach and record the fitness and propriety decision
actions: Bring together the declaration, screening results, credit assessment, references, interview record and qualification evidence into a single assessment record.
State the decision against each limb of the test: honesty and integrity and reputation, competence and capability, and financial soundness.
Where a concern exists, state the concern, the mitigation and why the individual is nonetheless fit and proper, or record the refusal.
Have the Nomination Committee record its recommendation for board and senior management function appointments.
checklist.done: a signed assessment record states a decision against all three limbs with concerns and mitigations recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the Form A application and wait for approval
actions: Complete the Form A long or short application on the FCA and PRA Connect portal with the individual's employment history, qualifications, declarations and the functions applied for.
Attach the Statement of Responsibilities, the updated Management Responsibilities Map and the candidate's curriculum vitae.
Track the statutory determination period and respond to any regulator information request within the date it states.
Confirm approval is granted and record the approval date before the individual starts performing the function.
checklist.done: Form A is submitted with attachments and a recorded approval date precedes the individual performing the function.

checklist.step: Prevent the individual performing the function before approval
actions: Set the start date for the function to the approval date, not the employment start date, and record both dates separately in the HR system.
Where the individual joins before approval, define in writing the duties they may and may not perform and who holds the function in the interim.
Update the Management Responsibilities Map on the approval date and have the individual sign their Statement of Responsibilities.
Confirm the Financial Services Register shows the individual against the function once approval is published.
checklist.done: function start date equals approval date, interim arrangements are written down, and the Register reflects the appointment.

checklist.step: Certify non-senior-manager roles and issue the certificate
actions: Maintain the population of certified roles and confirm each holder has a current assessment before a certificate is issued.
Issue the certificate stating the individual, the certified function and the validity period of no more than twelve months.
Record the certificate on the HR record and update the PRA Directory entry with the role, start date and customer-facing status.
Prevent the individual from performing the certified function where the certificate has lapsed and record the withdrawal.
checklist.done: every certified individual holds a current certificate recorded in HR and reflected in the Directory.

checklist.step: Run the annual reassessment for every in-scope individual
actions: Sixty days before each certificate anniversary, issue the annual declaration asking the individual to confirm or update every question from the original questionnaire.
Re-run the criminal record check where the role or the firm's policy requires it, and re-run the credit and adverse media screening annually.
Collect the conduct rule breach record and the performance and disciplinary record from the line manager for the year.
Record the reassessment decision before the certificate expiry date and renew or withdraw the certificate accordingly.
checklist.done: each individual has a dated annual reassessment and a renewal or withdrawal decision made before certificate expiry.

checklist.step: Reassess immediately on any change of circumstance
actions: Trigger reassessment on a conduct rule breach, a disciplinary finding, a regulatory investigation, a criminal charge, a bankruptcy or a director disqualification.
Suspend the individual from the function where the concern is serious, and record who performs the function in the interim.
Complete the reassessment inside 20 business days and record the outcome and the reasoning.
Notify the PRA where the outcome affects an approved person's fitness, and record the notification date.
checklist.done: each change of circumstance produces a reassessment inside 20 business days with an interim arrangement and any required notification.

checklist.step: Notify departures and provide references to other firms
actions: Submit Form C on Connect within 7 business days of a senior manager ceasing, stating the cessation date and whether any fitness concern arose.
Update the Directory entry within the required period for certified persons who cease their role.
Respond to inbound regulatory reference requests from other firms within six weeks, using the prescribed template and disclosing conduct breaches and fitness conclusions from the previous six years.
Have the Employment Counsel review any reference disclosing an adverse finding before it is sent.
checklist.done: Form C is filed within 7 business days and inbound reference requests are answered within six weeks with legal review of adverse content.

checklist.step: Report the fitness and propriety position to the Nomination Committee
actions: Report annually the population by category, the assessments completed, the certificates issued and withdrawn, the reassessments triggered and the outcomes.
Report every case where an individual was certified despite a concern, with the mitigation applied.
Report reference response times against the six-week standard and any reference outstanding beyond it.
Obtain committee acknowledgement and record the minute reference.
checklist.done: an annual committee report covers population, outcomes, concern cases and reference timeliness, with a recorded minute.

checklist.step: Retain the assessment records under the record-keeping rule
actions: Deposit the assessment record, declarations, screening results, references, interview notes, decision and Connect submissions per individual in a restricted-access folder.
Apply the retention label of 6 years after the individual ceases the role, extended to 10 years for senior management functions.
Confirm access is limited to HR, Legal, Compliance and Internal Audit, with the Data Protection Officer's retention and access basis recorded.
Confirm the record is retrievable by individual, function reference and assessment date for a regulator request.
checklist.done: each assessment file is stored with restricted access, the correct retention label and retrievability by individual and function.

testing.step: Build the population from HR and the public Register
actions: Extract every appointment, role change and cessation for directors, senior management functions, key function holders and certified persons in the period from the HR record.
Extract the firm's individuals from the Financial Services Register and the PRA Directory as at period start and period end.
Reconcile the two in both directions so an individual on the Register but not in HR, or the reverse, is surfaced as an exception.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction method and dates.
testing.done: the HR population and the public Register are reconciled in both directions with unmatched individuals listed.

testing.step: Reconcile certification status against the certified population
actions: List every role classified as certified and every individual holding one during the period, including movers and internal promotions.
Match each to a certificate with its issue and expiry dates and identify any period where the individual performed the function without a valid certificate.
Test the role classification itself on ten roles by reading the job description against the certification criteria, since misclassification removes people from the process entirely.
Record every uncertified period and every misclassified role as an exception.
testing.done: certified individuals are matched to valid certificates for their whole period and role classification is independently tested.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of individuals
actions: Take 100 per cent of senior management function appointments and cessations and 100 per cent of assessments recording an adverse finding.
Take 20 certified persons by seeded random selection across business areas from the remaining population.
Take all individuals whose assessment was triggered by a change of circumstance in the period.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all senior manager and adverse-finding cases plus a reproducible random selection of certified persons.

testing.step: Re-perform the assessment completeness check on each sampled file
actions: Open each sampled assessment file and confirm the presence and date of the declaration, criminal record certificate, credit check, sanctions and adverse media screening, qualification evidence and interview record.
Check the criminal record certificate is dated within three months of the appointment decision and that screening predates the decision, not follows it.
Confirm the decision record addresses all three limbs of the test explicitly rather than concluding with a single sentence.
Record any missing or post-dated element as a fail rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: each sampled file is checked element by element with every missing or post-dated screening recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Test regulatory reference coverage across the six-year period
actions: Build a timeline of the individual's declared employment for the six years before appointment from the curriculum vitae and the declaration.
Map every reference received onto the timeline and identify any regulated employment period with no reference and no documented alternative verification.
Confirm each reference used the prescribed template and answered the conduct and fitness questions rather than being a bare confirmation of dates.
Confirm any disclosed conduct breach was considered in the decision record and not simply filed.
testing.done: every regulated employment period in the six years is covered by a substantive reference or a documented alternative.

testing.step: Re-perform the approval date test against the function start date
actions: For each sampled senior management function, read the Connect approval date from the submission record and the Financial Services Register.
Compare it to the date the individual first performed the function, taken from the Management Responsibilities Map, board minutes and committee attendance rather than from HR alone.
Where the individual attended and voted at a meeting in the capacity of the function before approval, record it as performing the function.
Treat any performance before approval as a reportable breach requiring notification, not a test exception.
testing.done: approval dates are compared to actual first performance evidenced by minutes, with any pre-approval performance escalated.

testing.step: Recompute the notification and reference deadlines
actions: Recompute the 7 business day Form C deadline from each cessation date and compare it to the Connect submission timestamp.
Recompute the six-week deadline for each inbound regulatory reference request from the date it was received and compare it to the date the reference was sent.
Recompute the certificate expiry date and compare it to the date the renewal decision was recorded.
List every deadline missed with the number of days late.
testing.done: Form C, reference response and certificate renewal deadlines are recomputed and every miss is quantified in days.

testing.step: Test the handling of adverse findings and concern cases
actions: Read every sampled assessment where an adverse finding was disclosed and confirm the concern, the mitigation and the reasoning are all recorded.
Confirm the General Counsel sign-off exists and predates the appointment or certification decision.
Confirm any resulting supervision, restriction or development plan was actually implemented by checking the individual's subsequent record.
Treat a concern recorded with no reasoning, or a mitigation never implemented, as a fail.
testing.done: each adverse finding shows recorded reasoning, dated legal sign-off and evidence the mitigation was implemented.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the individual reference, the role, the missing element and the regulatory consequence, with access restricted for personal data.
Assign a root cause from role misclassified, screening ordered after the decision, reference not chased, renewal not scheduled, or cessation not notified.
Set an owner and a remediation date and require the file to be completed and retested in the next semi-annual cycle.
Escalate any pre-approval performance or lapsed certificate to the General Counsel within one business day for a notification decision.
testing.done: every exception has a restricted-access issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the file completeness rate, the reference coverage rate and the on-time notification rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the reviewer who conducted or approved no tested assessment sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and every breach to the Nomination Committee and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under restricted access.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with completeness and timeliness rates, a stated conclusion and dated committee reporting references.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Runs the annual policy approval cycle on behalf of the board; each written policy has its own executive owner (Chief Risk Officer for risk management, Chief Audit Executive for internal audit, Chief Financial Officer for internal control, Third-Party Risk Manager for outsourcing)

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 2.5 requiring written policies for risk management, internal control, internal audit and, where relevant, outsourcing, with prior board approval, review at least annually and update after any material change, read with Conditions Governing Business 5 for the internal audit policy

In-scope processes.value: Annual review and board approval of the mandated written policy set for the UK Life and Annuities entity, plus out-of-cycle re-approval after any material change to the business, the risk profile or the regulatory framework

In-scope systems.value: Approved policies, versions and board approval minutes are held in the board portal and the governance library; attestation and dissemination are tracked in the policy register

Compliance procedure documented.value: Policy Governance Procedure — policy inventory and owner mapping, annual review scheduling, gap assessment against the rulebook, committee pre-review, board approval, version publication, dissemination and attestation, and material-change re-approval

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board on the recommendation of the Board Risk Committee; reviewed annually alongside the policy set and re-approved on any change to the mandated policy list

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every mandated policy must be board-approved within 12 months of its last approval date; a material change triggers re-approval at the next board meeting and no later than 90 days from the change; the policy set supports the SFCR System of Governance disclosure at 31 December plus 70 business days

Deadline reminders configured.value: The policy register raises tasks at last approval plus 9, 10 and 11 months to the policy owner, the Board Governance Lead and the Corporate Secretary, and raises an immediate task on any material change logged in the regulatory or business change register

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every approved policy version, the review and gap assessment, the committee and board papers, the approval minute and the attestation record retained 10 years from the date the version was superseded

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any policy past 12 months without board approval, any material change not reflected within 90 days, any policy noted rather than approved, and any policy in force but not disseminated is logged with the policy and owner named

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The SMF1 Chief Executive Officer signs off the remediation plan for any lapsed policy and confirms the interim control arrangement until board approval is restored

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every policy in the mandated set for the entity, each version approved in the period, the board and committee minutes recording approval, and every material change logged in the change registers

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance: any mandated policy without board approval inside 12 months is a fail; any policy recorded as noted rather than approved is a fail; any material change not reflected within 90 days is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual with event-driven re-approval, so the test runs annually across the whole policy set after the approval cycle, with a half-year check on material changes and their re-approval timeliness

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside the secretariat and the policy owner functions and must not have drafted or sponsored any tested policy

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policy governance test workpaper (policy inventory, approval date recomputation, minute verification, content gap assessment, change traceability, attestation coverage, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Policy register showing each mandated policy, its current version, its board approval date and minute reference, with the approved documents attached, producible to a PRA supervisor within 3 business days
