checklist.step: Maintain the mandated policy inventory with an owner for each
actions: List every written policy Conditions Governing Business 2.5 requires: risk management, internal control, internal audit and outsourcing, plus the underlying risk policies for underwriting and reserving, asset-liability management, investment, liquidity and concentration, operational risk and reinsurance.
Record for each policy the executive owner, the approving body, the last approval date, the version number and the next due date.
Map each policy to the rulebook provision it satisfies so a supervisor can see the coverage without reading every document.
Flag any rulebook requirement with no policy assigned and open a drafting task with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: the inventory lists every mandated policy with owner, approving body, version, approval date, due date and rulebook mapping.

checklist.step: Schedule the annual review cycle so no policy passes twelve months
actions: Build the annual calendar placing each policy at a committee and board meeting no later than eleven months after its last approval.
Spread the set across the year so a single meeting does not receive fifteen policies and approve them without challenge.
Set the paper deadline at five business days before each meeting and notify each owner ninety days before their meeting date.
Publish the calendar to owners and committee chairs and track slippage weekly in the final quarter.
checklist.done: every policy has a scheduled committee and board date inside eleven months of its last approval, with owners notified.

checklist.step: Assess each policy against the current rulebook and supervisory expectations
actions: Read each policy against the specific rulebook provisions it maps to and against any PRA policy statement, supervisory statement or Dear CEO letter issued since the last approval.
Produce a gap assessment listing each requirement, whether the policy addresses it, and the paragraph that does so.
For the outsourcing policy, test coverage of material outsourcing identification, due diligence, contractual requirements, exit planning and regulatory notification.
Give each owner the gap list with a drafting deadline before the paper deadline.
checklist.done: each policy has a gap assessment mapping every requirement to a paragraph or to a named drafting action.

checklist.step: Have the owner update the policy content
actions: Update the policy to close each gap and to reflect changes in the business, the risk profile, the risk appetite statement and the organisational structure since the last version.
Confirm the policy states its scope, the roles accountable, the mandatory controls, the escalation route and the review frequency, rather than describing intent only.
Produce a redline against the approved version and a change summary naming every substantive change and why it was made.
Confirm cross-referenced documents, such as the risk appetite statement and the ORSA policy, are consistent with the update.
checklist.done: each policy is updated with a redline, a change summary and confirmed consistency with cross-referenced documents.

checklist.step: Test the policy against how the work is actually done
actions: Walk two or three key requirements of each policy through to the operating procedure and the control that implements them.
Where the policy requires something the business does not do, record the gap and choose deliberately between changing the practice and changing the policy.
Confirm every mandatory control named in the policy exists in the control library with an owner and a testing frequency.
Report unimplementable requirements to the policy owner before board approval rather than discovering them at the next audit.
checklist.done: sampled policy requirements are traced to real procedures and controls, with every unimplemented requirement recorded.

checklist.step: Take the internal audit policy through the Audit Committee
actions: Present the internal audit policy and charter to the Audit Committee, covering independence, unrestricted access to information and staff, reporting line to the committee chair and the right to audit any area including outsourced functions.
Confirm the policy states that internal audit performs no operational duties and that its remuneration is set independently of the areas it audits.
Record the committee's challenge and its recommendation to the board in the minute.
Confirm the audit plan approved separately is consistent with the scope the policy claims.
checklist.done: the internal audit policy is recommended by the Audit Committee with independence and access provisions minuted.

checklist.step: Take the risk and internal control policies through the Board Risk Committee
actions: Present the risk management policy covering each risk category the entity is exposed to, the appetite linkage, the measurement approach and the escalation thresholds.
Present the internal control policy covering the control framework, the three lines model, attestation and the reporting of control failures.
Record the committee's challenge on any weakened threshold or removed requirement, since dilution is the change that matters most.
Capture the committee recommendation to the board with any condition attached.
checklist.done: the risk and internal control policies carry a minuted committee recommendation with challenge on any diluted requirement.

checklist.step: Assemble the board approval pack
actions: Circulate at least five business days before the board: the policy, the redline, the change summary, the gap assessment and the committee recommendation.
State clearly on the cover sheet that board approval is sought under Conditions Governing Business 2.5, so the decision cannot be recorded as noting.
List any policy where approval is sought without a committee recommendation and explain why.
Confirm every director has portal access to the full pack before the deadline.
checklist.done: the board pack contains policy, redline, change summary, gap assessment and recommendation, circulated five business days ahead.

checklist.step: Obtain and minute the board approval precisely
actions: Have the minute record the policy name, the version number, the approval date and the words approved, not noted or received.
Record the challenge raised, any amendment required as a condition of approval and who must implement it by when.
Where the board approves subject to amendment, do not publish the policy until the amendment is made and confirmed to the chair.
Write the approval date and minute reference back to the policy register the same week.
checklist.done: each policy has a minute naming version, date and the word approved, with conditions tracked and the register updated.

checklist.step: Publish the approved version and retire the old one
actions: Publish the approved version with its new version number, approval date, owner and next review date on the front page.
Archive the superseded version as read-only so the history remains available for a supervisor or an auditor.
Remove or redirect every stale copy on team sites so only one authoritative version is reachable.
Confirm the policy register, the board portal and the document repository all show the same current version.
checklist.done: one authoritative published version exists, the prior version is archived read-only and all three registers agree.

checklist.step: Disseminate the policy and capture attestation
actions: Identify the audience for each policy from the role mapping and assign the read-and-attest task with a 30-day completion date.
Where the change is material, deliver a short briefing to the affected teams rather than relying on an attestation click.
Track completion by team and escalate non-completion to the line manager at day 20 and to the executive owner at day 30.
Record the attestation rate against each policy version in the policy register.
checklist.done: each policy version has an assigned audience, a tracked attestation with escalation, and a recorded completion rate.

checklist.step: Re-approve out of cycle when a material change occurs
actions: Assess every entry in the regulatory change log and the business change register for a material effect on a mandated policy, and record the assessment either way.

Where material, for example a new material outsourcing arrangement, a change in risk appetite or a new PRA expectation, update the policy and take it to the next board meeting and no later than 90 days from the change.
Where a change is judged not material, record the reasoning so the judgement can be tested later.
Log the trigger, the assessment date and the re-approval date against the policy in the register.
checklist.done: every logged change carries a recorded materiality assessment and material ones are re-approved within 90 days.

checklist.step: Report policy compliance to the board annually
actions: Report the full policy set with last approval date, version, days to next review, attestation rate and any policy past its twelve-month limit.
Report the material changes assessed in the year and how each was handled, including those judged not material.
Use the same content to support the internal control and risk management descriptions in SFCR section B so the disclosure matches the record.
Obtain board acknowledgement and record the minute reference.
checklist.done: a board-acknowledged annual report covers approval currency, attestation, material changes and SFCR alignment.

checklist.step: Escalate and control around any lapsed policy
actions: Where a policy passes twelve months without approval, escalate to the board chair within one business day with the reason and the recovery date.
Confirm in writing that the prior version remains in force and continues to be applied, so no control gap opens while approval is restored.
Approve the recovery plan and, where the lapse is material, agree whether the PRA supervisory contact should be told proactively.
Record the lapse, the interim arrangement and the recovery in the policy register and the risk system.
checklist.done: each lapse has a same-week escalation, a written interim arrangement, an approved recovery plan and a register entry.

checklist.step: File the policy governance evidence
actions: Deposit each approved policy version with its redline, change summary, gap assessment, committee and board papers, approval minute and attestation report.
Apply the 10-year retention label measured from the date the version was superseded so the full version history survives.
Confirm the record is searchable by policy name, version number, approval date and rulebook provision.
Grant read-only access to Internal Audit, the key function holders and the external auditor.
checklist.done: each policy version pack is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by policy, version and rulebook provision.

testing.step: Rebuild the mandated policy population from the rulebook, not the register
actions: List the policies Conditions Governing Business 2.5 and 5 require and the underlying risk policies the risk management system needs for the entity's risk profile.
Compare your list to the policy register and treat any required policy absent from the register as an automatic exception.
Search the document repository and team sites for policy documents in use that are not in the register, since unregistered policies escape the approval cycle entirely.
Sign the population as complete and record the sources searched.
testing.done: an independently derived policy population is reconciled to the register, with missing and unregistered policies listed.

testing.step: Recompute every approval anniversary and test currency
actions: Take the last board approval date for each policy from the board minutes rather than the register field.
Recompute the twelve-month anniversary and compare it to the next approval date actually achieved.
List every policy that spent any period beyond twelve months without approval and compute the days lapsed.
Treat every lapse as a fail regardless of whether the content was still fit for purpose.
testing.done: approval anniversaries are recomputed from minutes and every lapsed day is quantified per policy.

testing.step: Draw the sample of policies and versions
actions: Take 100 per cent of the four policies named in Conditions Governing Business 2.5 and 100 per cent of policies re-approved out of cycle.
Take eight further policies by seeded random selection from the remaining mandated set.
Take all policies with an attestation rate below 95 per cent.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all rulebook-named and out-of-cycle policies plus a reproducible random selection.

testing.step: Verify the approval in the minute rather than the register
actions: Open the board minute for each sampled approval and confirm it names the policy and the version number approved.
Confirm the minute records approval rather than noting, receiving or endorsing, since only approval satisfies the rule.
Where approval was conditional, confirm the condition was implemented and confirmed to the chair before publication.
Record any policy published before its condition was met as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled approval is evidenced by a minute naming the version and the word approved, with conditions verified.

testing.step: Re-perform the gap assessment on two policies
actions: Take the risk management policy and the outsourcing policy and independently map every applicable rulebook requirement to a policy paragraph.
Read the outsourcing policy specifically for material outsourcing identification, due diligence, contractual rights of access and audit, exit planning and regulatory notification.
Compare your mapping to the owner's gap assessment and list any requirement the owner marked as covered that you cannot find.
Treat an unaddressed rulebook requirement as a fail even where the practice happens to be adequate.
testing.done: two policies are independently mapped to the rulebook and every unsupported coverage claim is listed.

testing.step: Trace policy requirements to real controls and procedures
actions: Select five mandatory requirements across the sampled policies and identify the procedure and control that implements each.
Confirm each control exists in the control library with an owner, a frequency and evidence of recent operation.
Perform one walkthrough per requirement with the operating team to confirm the practice matches the policy text.
Record every requirement with no implementing control as a fail and quantify the exposure it leaves.
testing.done: each sampled requirement is traced to an operating control with evidence, or recorded as unimplemented.

testing.step: Test material-change identification and the 90-day re-approval
actions: Extract the regulatory change log, the business change register and the new material outsourcing arrangements agreed in the period.
Independently judge materiality for ten entries and compare your judgement to the recorded assessment, challenging any change judged immaterial without reasoning.
For each material change, recompute the 90-day deadline from the change date and compare it to the re-approval date.
Record any material change never assessed, or assessed and re-approved late, as a fail.
testing.done: materiality judgements are independently re-performed and every 90-day re-approval deadline is recomputed and tested.

testing.step: Test version control, publication and attestation coverage
actions: Confirm the version published in the repository is byte-identical to the version attached to the board paper approved.
Search team sites and shared drives for stale copies of the sampled policies still reachable by staff.
Compare the attestation audience to the role mapping and test whether joiners in the period were assigned the policy.
Record any published version differing from the approved version as a fail rather than a version-control nuisance.
testing.done: published versions match approved versions, stale copies are identified and attestation audiences are tested for completeness.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the policy, the version, the days lapsed or the unaddressed requirement.
Assign a root cause from calendar slippage, owner vacancy, minute recorded as noting, materiality assessment skipped, or publication not synchronised with approval.
Set an owner and a remediation date inside the next cycle and require the policy to be retested at the next annual test.
Escalate any lapsed mandated policy to the Chief Executive Officer within one business day for the interim control confirmation.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the approval currency rate, the rulebook coverage exception rate and the attestation rate against the zero-lapse threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective, citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the reviewer who drafted or sponsored no tested policy sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion, every lapsed policy and every unaddressed rulebook requirement to the Audit Committee and the board, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with currency, coverage and attestation rates, a stated conclusion and a dated committee reporting reference.
